item.title: Rams starter to finish the year on injured reserve
item.description: Yet another pass-catcher, Terrance Ferguson, is being shutdown by the Los Angeles Rams
item.content:encoded:
Bad injury news continues to hit the Los Angeles Rams this week, ahead of their next opponent, the Green Bay Packers. First, it was revealed that receiver Davante Adams will not be able to return from injured reserve to suit up against the Packers after both teams’ “mini-byes.” Now, tight end Terrance Ferguson will be shut down for the season.

According to Rams head coach Sean McVay, Ferguson, who had his practice window open on November 4th, hasn’t seen progress in his ankle injury. With his 21-day window wrapping up, Los Angeles is going to allow him to remain on the injured reserve — which will end his 2026 season. Ferguson will apparently undergo surgery to the injured ankle.

Between Adams, Ferguson and Puka Nacua, who is also on the injured reserve, the Rams’ pass-catching unit is taking hit after hit this year.

Currently, Los Angeles’ wide receivers are Konata Mumpfield (a 2025 seventh-round pick), Tutu Atwell (usually a returner), C.J. Daniels (a rookie sixth-round pick) and Xavier Smith (who was poached from the San Francisco 49ers’ practice squad in Week 10), for perspective.

What was once a strength of the team during Matthew Stafford’s 2025 MVP season is now a clear weakness.

item.title: DK Metcalf will not be suspended for actions during Steelers-Eagles
item.description: According to multiple reports, while Metcalf has avoided a suspension, he may still be fined.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers receiver DK Metcalf will not be suspended for his actions during Sunday's loss to the Eagles, according to multiple Monday reports.

Metcalf, however, may still be fined.

Metcalf was ejected for committing two unsportsmanlike conduct fouls over the course of the game.

Metcalf then left the locker room without speaking to reporters. But spoke to them on Monday, denying the accusation that he was trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

It’s been a trying year for Metcalf, who has just 36 catches for 434 yards with two touchdowns in 10 games. That the receiver will not be suspended is a positive development for him. But Pittsburgh would surely like to see Metcalf increase his production and reduce the on-field antics that do not help the team.

item.title: NFL news, live updates: 49ers release Brandon Aiyuk, reportedly extend GM John Lynch as team gets off to 9-1 start
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
Week 11 of the NFL season is almost completed with the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) and Washington Commanders (3-5-1) set to play on Monday night.

The week began with Thursday night's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans. The Texans prevailed 26-3 as the Colts performed so poorly offensively that the team decided to move on from quarterback Daniel Jones and released him the next day.

Jones' next destination will be one of the NFL's top stories as Week 11 finishes and the season progresses toward Week 12. The eight-year veteran is expected to clear waivers on Monday and from there, he will wait to see what his best option is, according to ESPN. Among the teams that could line up to sign him are the Arizona Cardinals, New England Patriots and Baltimore Ravens.

The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City to close out Sunday's slate. With the 35-10 victory, the Niners improved to 9-1 to keep hold of the top seed in the NFC. The Buffalo Bills matched them for the NFL's best mark with a 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

One concern for NFL coaches this week might be players celebrating touchdowns with backflips and front-flips. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo and Detroit Lions receiver Jameson Williams each went airborne in their Week 11 games, surely making their head coaches cringe. Teams have seven more weeks to keep their players on the ground.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

item.title: Patriots designate starting guard Alijah Vera-Tucker to return from injured reserve
item.description: A hamstring injury sent the March signing to injured reserve in October.
item.content:encoded:
As the New England Patriots headed back to work following the bye week, so did Alijah Vera-Tucker.

The starting left guard was present for Monday’s bonus practice inside the WIN Waste Innovations Field House. His 21-day activation window, in turn, has been opened at the earliest date that it could be.

Vera Tucker, 27, sustained a hamstring injury in October and was placed on injured reserve in the hours leading up to the team’s 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. The 6-foot-4, 308-pound offseason signing is now eligible to return to the 53-man roster in time for the final matchup of November after missing the NFL minimum of four games.

In the interim, New England’s interior offensive line depth includes Greg Van Roten, Matt Pryor, Walter Rouse and a previously scratched Ben Brown around starting center Jared Wilson. And with backup Tommy DeVito next up at quarterback in the fallout of captain Drake Maye’s fractured fibula.

“I think AVT’s got a chance to be out there,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters ahead of Monday’s practice, while also noting that wide receiver Romeo Doubs’ return from a shoulder injury could be near. “I think Romeo, maybe later in the week. Too soon to tell right now.”

Arriving on a three-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in March, Vera-Tucker stands six starts into his stay in Foxborough. He had played 100 percent of the offensive snaps before departing in the second quarter of what became a 26-19 win over his former New York Jets.

The USC product entered the NFL in the first round of the 2021 draft at No. 14 overall. Despite prior stints on injured reserve in 2022, 2023 and 2025, he stands 49 starts and 2,985 offensive downs into his AFC East career.

League rules permit eight return designations from injured reserve over the course of a regular season. Six of those eight have now been utilized by last year’s conference champions.

The Los Angeles Chargers host next Sunday’s flexed-out 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium.

item.title: Micah Parsons still needs clearance to play on Wednesday
item.description: Parsons’ family and friends have bought tickets to the game in Los Angeles
item.content:encoded:
Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur isn’t being very forward about the team’s injury situation leading up to their Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. File it under gamesmanship.

In the post-practice media availability in the locker room, though, edge defender Micah Parsons told the press that he still has one more hurdle he needs to jump before he’s allowed to play against the Rams this week: Final clearance from surgeon Dr. Neal ElAttrache.

ElAttrache, who did Parsons’ knee surgery, is widely considered the top knee expert for NFL players in the post-Dr. James Andrews era. According to Parsons, he will have a conference call with ElAttrache after media availability.

Parsons has been able to participate in all of the Packers’ practices this week without a knee brace. He also stated, according to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman, that friends and family of his have bought tickets to the games on Wednesday.

Things seem to be lining up for a Parsons return, but there’s still no official word on his status. The Packers won’t need to make a corresponding roster move for Parsons’ addition to the active roster, as the team released running back Pierre Strong Jr. (and later re-signed him to the practice squad) earlier this week. Presumably, that open roster spot will end up going to Parsons whenever he’s activated.

—

Update: Rams reporter Adam Grosbard of the Los Angeles Daily News is reporting that Rams edge defender Myles Garrett stated that Parsons requested extra tickets from Garrett for Wednesday’s game.

item.title: Steelers’ DK Metcalf dodges NFL suspension
item.description: Metcalf reportedly won’t be suspended after appearing to try and poke the Eagles’ Cooper DeJean in the eye on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf won’t be suspended by the NFL after an altercation in Sunday’s game against the Eagles, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Monday.

Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game after drawing his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty against the Eagles. Late in the third quarter, Metcalf appeared to try and poke the eyes of Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean.

Schefter reported Metcalf’s conduct will still be reviewed “for discipline in the form of fines.”

By avoiding suspension, Metcalf dodges missing games for disciplinary reasons for the second straight season in Pittsburgh. In 2025, Metcalf was suspended for the Steelers’ last two games of the season after an altercation with a fan when playing the Lions in Detroit.

The veteran receiver denied trying to poke DeJean in the eyes.

“I didn’t poke him in the eye … I was telling him to stop pushing me,” Metcalf told the media Monday, per PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh.

In his Monday press conference, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he had “productive” conversations with Metcalf, per ESPN’s Brooke Pryor.

Metcalf finished the Eagles game with one catch for two yards.

item.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf reportedly won't be suspended, denies he tried to poke Eagles' Cooper DeJean in the eye
item.description: "You said I tried to what?" Metcalf responded when asked about the alleged eye poke.
item.content:encoded:
DK Metcalf says he didn't try to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

He also won’t be serving a suspension. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the NFL won’t suspend the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver following his ejection from Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Per the report, Metcalf could still be subject to a fine.

Metcalf was ejected due to two personal fouls, both related to scuffles with DeJean, a cornerback for the Eagles. Per Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, a referee told him that Metcalf "poked a defender in the eye."

Metcalf didn't speak with media after the 19-16 loss. He was available at his locker on Monday and confirmed to reporters that "I was avoiding y'all" on Sunday. This was prior to the report that he won’t be suspended.

'You said I tried to what?'

Here's Metcalf’s response when asked about "when you tried to poke Cooper in the eye."

"You said I tried to what?" Metcalf responded. "I didn't try to poke him in the eye. … I was just telling him to stop pushing me. That's all I said."

#Steelers DK Metcalf on the Cooper DeJean eye poke:

— Jimmy Scoops (@jimkryjer) November 23, 2026

Here's video of the altercation that led to Metcalf's second personal foul penalty and ejection. The video shows Metcalf with his right hand pushing at DeJean's facemask. It's taken from a distance and blurry.

DK Metcalf has been ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Not seen in the above clip, Metcalf also grabbed the facemask of Eagles safety Andrew Mukuba and shoved his head back. He also swiped at the arm of an official when the official put his hand on his chest to try to separate Metcalf from the scrum.

What DeJean said

As for the alleged eye poke, DeJean told reporters after the game that Metcalf "just missed" poking him in the eye.

"Almost, almost," DeJean said when asked if he got poked in the eye. "He just missed. … We were just competing. Things like that happen in football.

"It wasn't anything crazy. Nobody was really saying anything, two guys were going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me. Things like that. Obviously it carried over to whatever that was at the end."

Cooper DeJean laughed off the scrum with D.K. Metcalf in the win over the Steelers.

On Monday, Metcalf declined to offer details of his side of the altercations beyond denying that he tried to poke DeJean in the eye.

"Can't remember," he responded when asked what happened between him and DeJean. "You've gotta ask him."

Metcalf has history

This is not the first time Metcalf has been accused of poking or trying to poke an opponent in the eye.

During a Week 8 game in 2025, Walker was penalized and later fined $12,172 for this incident in which he stuck a finger inside the facemask of Packers linebacker Quay Walker.

It's not clear as of Monday if Metcalf will receive further discipline from the NFL for Sunday's incidents against the Eagles.

Metcalf is in his second season with the Steelers after six seasons with the Seahawks that featured two Pro Bowl selections. His first season in Pittsburgh produced the lowest output of his career, 59 catches for 850 yards and 6 touchdowns.

Through 10 games this season, Metcalf is on pace to fall short of those season-long numbers with 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns. He had one catch for two yards at the time of his ejection Sunday late in the third quarter.

item.title: DK Metcalf “can’t remember” what happened with Cooper DeJean that led to his ejection
item.description: The Steelers WR took no responsibility for losing his cool against the Eagles on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles finally snapped a seven-game losing streak on Sunday against the Steelers, and it was a physical game from the start. Things escalated quickly between Philly DB Cooper DeJean and Pittsburgh WR DK Metcalf, with the latter eventually ejected after a pair of personal foul penalties — including one for poking DeJean in the eyes.

Metcalf was escorted off the field, he got dressed, and left the stadium without speaking to reporters about the incident. He wasn’t able to avoid questions on Monday, however, but the WR didn’t offer much of an explanation. When asked what happened against DeJean, Metcalf said, “Can’t remember.”

He deferred to his opponents to answer for his actions, and also denied poking DeJean in the eyes — despite the video showing him doing just that. Metcalf refused to take any accountability for how he reacts to being provoked, which is a very frequent issue for him, and said that he just wishes he was able to be there for his teammates.

As for DeJean, the Eagles DB didn’t seem all too worried about the dustup, and after the game, took the high road about the situation.

“We were just competing. You know, things like that happen in football. Wasn’t anything crazy. No one was really saying anything. It was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off of me, things like that, and that obviously carries over to whatever that was…when he got thrown out.”

DeJean said he wasn’t trying to play agitator out there, and said he wasn’t aware of how many times Metcalf has been ejected heading into the game.

“But he wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game and some receivers, that gets to them. Obviously, tried to take it out on me.”

Ultimately, Metcalf left the game with more penalties than receptions, and will probably face some kind of punishment from the league.

… but apparently not in the form of a suspesnion.

item.title: 49ers, general manager John Lynch reportedly agree to multiyear contract extension
item.description: Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed on the new contract with a handshake on the sideline before the 49ers' game in Mexico City.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multiyear contract extension with the team, according to reports.

Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the new contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

Exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially announced the agreement. Lynch's contract was set to expire after this season.

Lynch's new deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

The 49ers' general manager and head coach have been working in tandem since 2017. both originally signing six-year contracts. Lynch had been a broadcast analyst for Fox Sports for the previous eight years. In 2023, he agreed to a three-year contract extension and was also named president of football operations.

Under Lynch and Shanahan, the 49ers have compiled a 91-68 record, including four seasons of 12 or more wins and two NFC championships. (San Francisco lost Super Bowls 54 and 58, both to the Kansas City Chiefs.)

Prior to his broadcasting career, Lynch played 15 NFL seasons for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (who drafted him in the third round out of Stanford) and Denver Broncos. As a safety, he was named to nine Pro Bowls and earned All-Pro honors four times (two first-team, two second-team).

Lynch is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame, Buccaneers' Ring of Honor and the Broncos' Ring of Fame for his accomplishments as a player.

As an executive, Lynch has not been afraid to make bold moves to build a winner in San Francisco. Key pieces he acquired in trades include left tackle Trent Williams and running back Christian McCaffrey.

In the draft, Lynch moved up to select quarterback Trey Lance in 2021 with the No. 3 overall pick. That decision didn’t work out, but he made up for it by picking current QB Brock Purdy, playing like an MVP candidate, with the final pick of the 2022 draft.

This season, he signed receiver Mike Evans and made deals to acquire defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wideout Keenan Allen.

San Francisco appears to be on its way to another campaign of at least 12 victories, currently tied for the best record in the NFL at 9-1. The team has seven regular-season games remaining, including matchups with the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8), Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) and Arizona Cardinals (3-8).

item.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
item.description: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.

Head coach John Harbaugh said at his Monday press conference that Newsome suffered a high-ankle sprain. Harbaugh said that Newsome will be out multiple weeks as a result of the injury.

Newsome only played four snaps before being forced out of Sunday's game. He has 35 tackles, an interception and eight passes defensed in his nine appearances this season.

That play earned Newsome a three-year extension beyond the one-year deal he signed with the team in the offseason, but the Giants will have to turn elsewhere in the secondary for the near future.

item.title: Dennard Wilson interviews for Maryland job in potential Giants complication
item.description: In the wake of the Giants’ biggest win of the season, John Harbaugh may soon be faced with a devastating loss.
item.content:encoded:
In the wake of the Giants’ biggest win of the season, John Harbaugh may soon be faced with a devastating loss.

First-year defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson — whose top-10 defense has led the Giants (6-3-1) to first place in the NFC East — recently conducted a virtual interview for the vacant head-coaching position at the University of Maryland, according to an ESPN/NFL Network report.

Access the Giants like never before

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

tRY IT NOW

On Monday, Harbaugh told reporters there was “no level of concern” that the situation would interrupt the season, nor that Wilson would leave in the middle of the season.

“We’re getting ahead of ourselves,” he said, noting that if Wilson were to get an offer, they’d cross that bridge “when we get there.”

Wilson, 44, is a Maryland native who was a defensive back for the Terrapins and spent two years (2007-08) as a graduate assistant with the program, which fired eighth-year head coach Mike Locksley last month.

Maryland is currently being led by interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim, the former co-defensive coordinator.

Wilson got his first NFL job as a defensive quality control coach with the Rams in 2012, and spent time with five other teams, including a four-year stint (2017-20) as a defensive assistant with the Jets.

After working for Harbaugh as Baltimore’s defensive backs coach in 2023, Wilson spent two years as Tennessee’s defensive coordinator, before reuniting with Harbaugh on the Giants this year.

Wilson’s defense is coming off its best performance of the season, in which it held the Jaguars’ fourth-ranked offense to its second-lowest point total (18) of the year. The Giants are currently tied for seventh in total defense.

item.title: Greg Newsome injury: Giants CB out multiple weeks with ankle injury
item.description: Coach John Harbaugh says Newsome suffered a high ankle sprain against the Jacksonville Jaguars
item.content:encoded:
New York Giants starting cornerback Greg Newsome will be out multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday.

Newsome left Sunday’s 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars after playing only four snaps. He was replaced by Paulson Adebo, who ended up with an interception and four passes defensed.

Harbaugh did not say whether Newsome would undergo surgery or be placed on injured reserve.

A 2021 first-round pick by the Cleveland Browns, Newsome signed a one-year contract with the Giants in free agency this past offseason after a couple of sub-par years with the Browns and Jaguars.

The 26-year-old has had a resurgent season with the Giants. His passer rating against of 67.3 is the best of his six-year NFL career. His completion percentage against of 57.9 is just a percentage point off his career-best.

Newsome was rewarded with a three-year, $45.75 million contract extension recently. That deal runs through the 2029 season.

"Monday Night Football" serves up an intriguing showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders, with one team looking to keep its foot on the gas and the other desperately trying to prove its season isn't six feet under.

Washington enters Monday night with a little extra breathing room after knocking off the New York Giants on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 10. Make no mistake, that was a must-win game for Dan Quinn's squad. With their season seemingly on life support, the Commanders have suddenly found a pulse and are right back in the NFC East race.

Unfortunately for Washington, the Bengals aren't exactly the team you want to run into when you're trying to build some momentum. Cincinnati is riding a five-game winning streak after absolutely dismantling the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Joe Burrow is making a serious push for NFL MVP honors.

During the Bengals' current winning streak, Burrow has thrown for 1,624 yards and 20 touchdowns, averaging a ridiculous 324.8 passing yards per game. He entered Week 11 leading the NFL with 27 touchdown passes and ranks second with 2,795 passing yards.

And Burrow has plenty of help. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins continue to make life miserable for opposing defensive backs, giving Cincinnati the most dangerous offensive passing attack in football.

Still, Washington shouldn't be counted out just yet. Jayden Daniels and the Commanders have dealt with plenty of adversity this season, but they're beginning to show flashes of the team many expected them to be.

Can Burrow, Chase and Higgins keep running roughshod, or will Daniels and Washington finally put together back-to-back wins for the first time this season?

item.title: NFC South Week 11 Review: The division leader no longer has a losing record
item.description: The Panthers stand alone.
item.content:encoded:
The division still doesn’t have a winning team, but a .500 lead is all the Panthers need to stand above the rest. The Buccaneers looked no better off their bye week; the Saints continue to sink, and the Falcons managed to gain ground while on their bye.

Here’s the Week 11 NFC South Review.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7)

Week 11 Result: Buccaneers 21 – Lions 31

Week 12 Opponent: Carolina Panthers 

The Lions took an early lead and never gave it back. Baker Mayfield is finally throwing the football again, but he’s piling up negative plays at a ridiculous rate. The quarterback is playing through a foot injury, but at this point that might be hurting the team more than anything. The run game and defense weren’t as potent today, and winning through the air just hasn’t been an option for the Buccaneers, who needed to keep pace with Detroit.

Sitting four games under .500 doesn’t matter in this division; Tampa Bay has a chance to gain significant ground when they host the Panthers on Monday.

Carolina Panthers (5-5)

Week 11 Result: Panthers 35 – Ravens 33

Week 12 Opponent: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 

This was the most chaotic game from the morning slate. The Ravens jumped out to an early 12-point lead, scoring a safety, touchdown, and field goal. The Panthers fought back and held off their feisty opponent, thanks to a critical Justice Hill fumble at the one-yard line.

Still, the Panthers made clutch plays when they had to, and now they sit in first place as the only team without a losing record. They have a chance to go over .500 and take a commanding lead in the division on Monday Night Football in Tampa Bay.  

New Orleans Saints (3-7)

Week 11 Result: Saints 13 – Bears 21

Week 12 Opponent: Cincinnati Bengals

The score was close, but the Bears were playing with their food. The Saints had chance after chance to steal this game, but botched every opportunity. New Orleans had two turnovers (an interception and a fumble) and a safety. Tyler Shough didn’t have to lead the team in rushing today, but his 42 attempts through the air led them to another loss.

Kellen Moore looks like a lemon; his offense is a wreck, and the Saints’ defense is no better. This team sits in last place and has another tough road game against the ferocious Bengals.

Atlanta Falcons (3-7)

Week 11 Result: Bye Week

Week 12 Opponent: Minnesota Vikings

The Falcons gained ground during the bye week and moved up to third in the rankings. That’s the most positive outcome they’ve had in weeks, and it perfectly sums up the season the Falcons have had so far. I know people are tired of hearing it and already window shopping draft picks, but the Falcons can turn this season around and win some games. While fans may want a tank, these players’ league reputations and contract incentives are on the line. This team’s heart will be tested immediately with a road game in Minnesota, against a familiar face in Kirk Cousins. 

We’ll learn a lot about this division next week. Carolina has a path to lock up this division by late December, and it starts on Monday against Tampa Bay, while the rest of the division eyes a chance to play spoiler. Nothing is certain in this division, and narratives can change on a dime.

item.title: Cowboys vs Titans: 1 player sets records in dominant performance
item.description: Dak Prescott was incredible on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
If the Dallas Cowboys wanted to keep their slim playoff hopes alive, they needed to beat the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon. Thankfully, Dallas took care of business, blowing out the Titans in a 51-30 victory.

For the first time all year, we saw Dallas’ defense play competent football throughout the course of the game. While there is no denying the defense played better, the Cowboys offense was the star of the show.

Dallas’ offense looked unstoppable from their opening drive, scoring six straight touchdowns on their first six offensive drives. A few offensive players had standout performances, but none shined brighter than Dak Prescott. Dallas’ signal-caller was at his best on Sunday, earning him this week’s game ball award.

You could make a solid argument that Sunday was the most efficient performance of Dak Prescott’s 11-year career. Prescott led all quarterbacks on Sunday in passing yards (325), passing touchdowns (4), completion percentage (84.8%), and Passer Rating (147.3). 

The veteran also recorded an unbelievable 0.709 EPA/Play to go with an 80.6% success rate, both the highest of any quarterback in Week 11. Dallas’ lead man made some history with his dominant performance, becoming the fourth QB in NFL history with at least 300 passing yards and five total touchdowns in consecutive games.

He also tied his own personal record of completing 19 consecutive passes in the game, something he also accomplished in the 2023 season.

If Prescott is going to keep playing like he has the past two weeks, the Cowboys are going to have a shot at beating any team they play the rest of the season. Sunday showed us just how dangerous Dallas can be if they get close to average play from their defense. Here’s to hoping they can keep it up and let their offense continue to lead the way moving forward.

item.title: Rams’ 2025 draft fallout is becoming impossible to ignore
item.description: The Rams 2025 draft class, not 2026 is the real issue…
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams are beginning to feel the consequences of what could go down as one of the worst drafts of the Sean McVay era. More than a year after selecting six players in the 2025 NFL Draft, the organization has received remarkably little production from the class. While some players are still developing, others have already fallen out of the team’s plans. And perhaps the biggest consequence is what the Rams passed on while making those selections.

Los Angeles has received little return on its investment in the 2025 draft class. Chris Paul failed to make the roster in 2025, while running back Jarquez Hunter was traded at the end of the 2026 preseason. Tight end Terrance Ferguson has been inactive for more than half of his career, and defensive end Josiah Stewart has already lost playing time to undrafted free agent Wesley Bailey.

Defensive tackle Ty Hamilton has barely seen the field in 2026 after not appearing in a single game as a rookie. Meanwhile, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield has accumulated just 335 receiving yards throughout his career.

That’s an underwhelming return from an entire draft class. However, the lack of production is only part of the problem. The biggest issue with the Rams’ 2025 draft might not be who they selected. It’s who they passed on.

Los Angeles had an opportunity to address its wide receiver position with young talent. Instead, the organization passed on several intriguing options, including Matthew Golden and Luther Burden III. Golden was available late in the first round, and the Rams potentially could have moved up four spots to secure his services. Burden, meanwhile, fell into the second round before being selected by the Chicago Bears.

Both represented opportunities to add a young, ascending receiver to an offense that would eventually need one. That decision is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The Rams are feeling the effects of not having a young wide receiver developing behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. With injuries and availability becoming an ongoing concern, having another legitimate receiving option could have made a significant difference. Instead, Los Angeles has been forced to look elsewhere for answers at a position that could have been addressed during the 2025 draft.

Perhaps the most frustrating part of the Rams’ recent draft strategy is their investment in the tight end position. Los Angeles selected Ferguson in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft before going back to the position in the second round of the 2026 draft with Max Klare. Ferguson has struggled to establish himself as a consistent contributor, while Klare has hardly played during his rookie season. Rather than adding another potential weapon at wide receiver, the Rams have now spent consecutive second-round selections on tight ends who have yet to provide meaningful production.

That doesn’t mean either player is destined to fail. Young players deserve time to develop, and draft evaluations shouldn’t be finalized after one or two seasons.

The Rams are trying to build a roster capable of competing for another Super Bowl, but their 2025 draft class has provided very little help toward that goal. More importantly, the organization passed on opportunities to address a position that is now becoming a significant concern. For the Rams, the fallout from 2025 is no longer just about missed evaluations. It’s about the talent they could have had, the roster holes they still need to fill, and the opportunities they may have wasted.

item.title: Mike McCarthy doesn't mince words when asked if he thought about a QB change: 'Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback'
item.description: Rodgers and the Steelers are coming off a loss to the 3-7 Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback."

Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

The Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

In the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

Pittsburgh is averaging 310.4 yards per game, the 10th-fewest in the league. The Steelers are also scoring 21.3 points per game, the 11th-fewest in the NFL.

Rodgers will turn 43 on Dec. 2 and has repeatedly said this will be his final season in the NFL. Through 10 games, the veteran QB has thrown for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

If the Steelers did want to make a change at quarterback, they don't have an obvious option.

Mason Rudolph is Rodgers' direct backup. He hasn't started consistently since 2024, when he was with the Tennessee Titans. Rudolph went 1-4 as a starter and threw for 1,530 yards, 9 touchdowns and 9 interceptions.

If Pittsburgh opted not to go with a veteran quarterback under center, the Steelers would get a look at their two young quarterbacks.

Pittsburgh drafted Will Howard in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft and Drew Allar in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Both are likely in contention to be the team's starter next year if/when Rodgers moves on, but neither has seen regular-season action.

For now, the Steelers will focus on ending their losing streak against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, and are expected to do so with Rodgers still as the team's starting QB.

item.title: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after latest blowout
item.description: The Cardinals aren't waiting until the offseason to make changes, as defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was fired Monday after the team's latest loss.
item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Cardinals aren't waiting until the offseason to start making changes.

The team on Monday fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, according to multiple reports.

First-year coach Mike LaFleur opted to keep Rallis, who had served in the role since 2023 under former coach Jonathan Gannon. Upon his hiring at 29, he became the NFL's youngest coordinator at the time.

But after Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Cardinals dropped to 3-8 and now rank 31st in scoring defense at 29.4 points allowed per game. At -132, Arizona has the NFL's worst point differential by a 34-point margin.

Rallis is just the second NFL coordinator to be fired this season. The Carolina Panthers dismissed defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Oct. 30.

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator. With more than 20 years of NFL coaching experience, Austin served as the Pittsburgh Steelers' defensive coordinator from 2022-25 before Mike Tomlin stepped down.

The Cardinals host the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

This story will be updated.

item.title: Tea leaves read as Klint Kubiak set to name Raiders’ new defensive starter
item.description: Kubiak may not admit it, but his actions are louder than his words.
item.content:encoded:
Klint Kubiak stopped short Monday of naming rookie Jermod McCoy the Raiders’ starting cornerback opposite Eric Stokes. But if actions speak louder than words, what Kubiak did Sunday in Denver tells you that might be exactly where this is headed.

Getting the start was one thing. Keeping it for more than 70 snaps was another.

In previous weeks, the Raiders had rotated McCoy, Zeke Masses and Darien Porter at that spot, sometimes changing corners in the middle of a game. 

Against the Broncos, Kubiak put McCoy out there and let him play.

“We got a room full of really solid players, but yesterday, we wanted to get a bigger look at Jmod,” Kubiak said.

McCoy had earned that look over the past few weeks. Whether he earned another one Sunday is a question Kubiak left open.

“I think it’ll be an ongoing discussion this week,” Kubiak said. “I won’t say yes or no right now.”

There is also the best-case scenario to consider: McCoy, Masses and Porter being the cornerstones of the Raiders’ secondary. All three are in their second or first years in the NFL.

But that is a story for another day.

There was a time when the idea of getting McCoy in the fourth round would have seemed more far-fetched than the idea of starting him as a rookie. As a sophomore at Tennessee in 2024, he intercepted four passes, earned All-America honors, and had a legitimate claim as the best cornerback in college football.

Then he tore his ACL during a workout in January 2025. He made it back to practice that August. But he never played another down for Tennessee.

The question for NFL teams went beyond when McCoy could play again. How long would the knee hold up once he did? As a result, a potential top-10 pick was still on the board when the third round ended. The Raiders traded up to take him with the first pick of the fourth, No. 101 overall.

Much of McCoy’s rookie season has gone into the two jobs that came with that pick. On the field, he had a year’s worth of rust to shake off. Imagine trying to recover a cornerback’s feel for when a receiver is about to break, only now the guy selling you the route makes his living doing it.

Away from the field, McCoy and the Raiders’ training staff had a longer view to take. Getting his knee ready for Sundays was part of it. So was figuring out what he could do week after week to keep it strong and give himself the best chance at a long career. Kubiak said that work was a priority from the start of training camp.

“He just continues to impress us with how he handles his body and how he gets his body ready to play,” Kubiak said.

The payoff in Denver was that Kubiak could leave McCoy on the field long enough to see him handle the demands of the job. For a kid who spent all of last season trying to get back into a game, that’s a different conversation to be having on a Monday. This one is about whether the job should be his.

item.title: 3 numbers that explain the Packers’ passing game in 2026
item.description: Let’s see the numbers that confirm what your eyes tell you about the Packers’ offense.
item.content:encoded:
Thanksgiving week is the time of the NFL season that many services start to offer up free trials or discounts. Perhaps the most notable is NFL Sunday Ticket, which has a massive promotional deal for the rest of the season this week.

But one promotion that’s notably free is at FTN, the online publication that is home to DVOA. While DVOA numbers remain behind their paywall, FTN has opened up its StatsIQ database to anyone with a user account on the site, and it has a wealth of statistics dating back to the 2023 season.

As a bit of a number cruncher myself, I immediately went on to the site to see if there was anything I could glean about the Green Bay Packers’ performance this season, particularly as far as the team’s offense is concerned. Unsurprisingly, I found a number of interesting indicators of the team’s struggles to protect Jordan Love and why, despite being under nearly constant pressure, he is still on a relatively short list of MVP candidates with seven weeks to go in the season.

It’s not just the numbers from this season that are notable, either; it’s the contrast that becomes visible when looking at the difference from 2025 to 2026. Let’s examine three areas that help illustrate why the Packers’ passing game looks and functions the way it has so far this season.

Average Time to Pressure

Unsurprisingly, the Packers’ offensive line is drastically affecting the function of the Packers’ passing game, and obviously it is doing so negatively. Love is tied with Justin Herbert for the third-fastest average time to pressure in the NFL this year at 2.44 seconds, with the only two faster being Patrick Mahomes (2.43) and Jameis Winston (2.41). That has sped up Love’s clock in the pocket, as he’s the NFL’s fastest quarterback in average time to throw (2.30 seconds).

Compare that against last season and the impact of the line is obvious. In 2025, Love’s time to pressure was 2.80 seconds, more than a third of a second longer, and his time to throw averaged 2.74 seconds. Both of those numbers were 10th-longest in the league, and they were each very close to his numbers in 2024 and 2023 as well.

Opposing rushers are getting to Love only a little bit more this season according to the raw pressure rate numbers (30.1% pressure rate in 2026 compared to rates around 28% in each of the past two years), but they are doing it much more quickly, and Love has had to deliver the football far faster than in years past. Surely, if he were still holding the ball longer and had an average time to throw on par with the last few years, that pressure rate would have spiked much more than it has so far.

Depth of Target

And yet, despite his clock accelerating, Love is averaging deeper throws this year than he has in the past. In 2024 and 2025, Love’s average depth of target (aDOT) was 8.8 yards, putting him around 4th or 5th in the NFL; this season he has increased that by more than a half-yard to 9.4, matching C.J. Stroud for the league’s top spot.

It’s actually quite impressive that he’s averaging deeper throws than last season despite his clock speeding up. Deeper routes typically need more time to develop, so one would think that Love would be focusing on more short passes. Instead, he’s putting the ball up with regularity and letting his speedy wide receivers run under them.

To that end, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both rank in the top five in total air yards on passes targeting them, with Golden first in the NFL and Watson fifth. Some of that is target volume; Watson is 10th in aDOT and Golden is 17th, but Golden ranks third in the NFL in total targets. Watson, meanwhile, has the highest yards per target of any player with 45 or more targets this season.

Love is facing pressure quickly and lofting deep balls quickly to his top receivers, confident that they’ll run under them and make the catch. Most of the time they do, but sometimes…

Drops

The numbers bear out the eye test on the 2026 Packers in terms of drops. No quarterback has seen his receivers drop a higher proportion of his passes than Jordan Love, who has seen 6.5% of his passes hit teammates’ hands before hitting the turf. The only quarterback dating back to 2023 with a higher drop rate over a whole season was Trevor Lawrence last year at a whopping 7.3%.

But not only are the Packers’ receivers dropping passes, they’re dropping meaningful passes. Love leads the league in air yards erased by dropped passes with 235, putting him on pace for 400 over a 17-game season. That would blow Lawrence’s 2025 number out of the water, as he lost 339 yards to drops. Love targeting players downfield more is a factor, but even Lawrence was near the top of the aDOT leaderboard last year, suggesting that the Packers are dropping deeper passes, on average, than the Jaguars did last year.

Unsurprisingly, Golden has been the biggest culprit among the Packers’ receivers. His 146 air yards lost due to drops make him the only player in triple digits so far this season. Notably, Detroit’s Jameson Williams had 154 yards lost to drops a year ago, but he and Golden are the only players to exceed 130 in a season since 2023.

It’s clear when you watch a game that the Packers’ passing game looks different than it did a year ago. But just imagine what this unit could look like if it had a more consistently competent offensive line blocking for Love and if the receivers — Matthew Golden in particular — could shake their issues with drops.

Packers fans saw a glimpse of the possibilities two games ago when the Packers dismantled the Patriots 45-27. Even though the Patriots’ pressure rate was higher than Love’s season average, their averate time to pressure was significantly slower at 2.59 seconds. That bought Love enough time to hit on some deep balls, as he had a whopping 13.2 aDOT in the game en route to a phenomenal performance.

That version of the passing game is certainly there. The Packers need to find a way to give Love just enough time to make it happen.

item.title: Chargers Week 11 PFF Grades: Pair of rookie OL impress despite loss
item.description: Logan Taylor was the team’s top offensive lineman vs. the Jets while Joe Alt was not far behind.
item.content:encoded:
Rookies Jake Slaughter and Logan Taylor were both forced into the starting lineup for the Chargers much earlier than either likely expected. Against the Jets, the two put on strong performances that should help ease the minds of Chargers fans who remain worried about the front five and the future depth of the group.

Taylor, a sixth-round pick out of Boston College, had his best best overall game against the Jets and finished Sunday as the team’s highest-graded offensive linemen. Slaughter, on the other hand, posted his second-best game grade of the year, trailing his current high mark by less than half a grade point.

Unfortunate it was the defense — for once — that let the whole team down on a night they failed to make the Jets punt even once. Hard to win any game when the complementary football is nowhere to be found.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Sunday.

Offense

Best

RB Keaton Mitchell – 89.5
OG Logan Taylor – 78.9
OT Joe Alt – 76.4
WR Ladd McConkey – 71.4
C Jake Slaughter – 68.6
RB Omarion Hampton – 68.6
QB Justin Herbert – 68.6

Mitchell played just two snaps against the Jets so his grade is a bit misleading, but he otherwise caught his lone pass of the game for a first down so at least that’s good efficiency!

Taylor ended up being the best offensive lineman against the Jets, beating out Alt by a couple grade points. He posted the team’s best run block grade at 77.6 to go with the third best pass block grade (69.2).

Alt led the way in pass protection with a 85.9 while his run block grade of 67.1 was third.

McConkey finally returned — and stayed — on the field for the entire game and wound up scoring two touchdowns whiling leading the team in both receptions and yards.

Slaughter, Hampton, and Herbert all played some of the their best football this year against New York. It was Herbert first game all year with multiple touchdown passes on top of committing no turnovers.

Worst

TE Oronde Gadsden – 46.6
OT Travis Burke – 53.0
OG Kayode Awosika – 53.2
WR Quentin Johnston – 55.8
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 56.2

Burke had very rough outing this week while facing Jets rookie pass rusher David Bailey who was this year’s third-overall pick. He allowed a sack (three pressures total) and ended with a 47.8 pass block grade.

Awosika was actually really good in pass pro against the Jets (82.0) but his run blocking left a lot to be desired as he finished with a 52.0. Somehow, that balanced out to a 53.2.

Johnston caught one pass on two targets for nine yards. His fall into irrelevancy continues.

Defense

Best
LB Troy Dye – 82.7
EDGE Bud Dupree – 79.6
CB Deane Leonard – 79.4
EDGE Caleb Murphy – 78.6
DT Justin Eboigbe – 69.6

Dye recorded the defense’s only sack while being only one of two players to record multiple pressures. His pass rush grade of 87.4 was by far the best on the team.

Leonard’s 81.0 coverage grade was tops on the team and the next best among defensive backs was nearly 20 full points lower (Tony Jefferson, 62.2).

Murphy had the defense’s second best coverage grade (76.2) and landed among the top six in both run defense (66.4) and tackling (73.9).

Eboigbe’s 71.4 run defense grade second on the team only to safety Elijah Molden.

Worst

CB Donte Jackson – 28.1
DT Teair Tart – 29.1
DT Dalvin Tomlinson – 38.5
S Genesis Smith – 42.2
S R.J. Mickens – 46.3

Jackson would probably like to forget Sunday’s performance as soon as possible. He finished with five catches allowed for 71 yards and three touchdowns. He also missed a pair of tackles. Not great!

Tart posted a 29.0 run defense grade, marking his worst performance of the season in that area. His pass rush grade of 52.2 was also tied for worst on the team.

Smith posted the second worst tackling (27.6) and coverage grades (40.1) for the Chargers. He missed two tackles, well.

Mickens finsihed with poor marks across the board with lowlights coming in coverage (49.6) and tackling (42.5).

item.title: PFF grades and advanced stats from the Giants’ 23-18 victory over the Jaguars
item.description: An outstanding performance by the defense is obvious in the stats
item.content:encoded:
This Sunday felt like a turning point for the New York Giants’ season and for the franchise in general. They’d gotten off to a good start, but against bad to mediocre teams. The best team they had played had beaten them soundly, and they’d lost two games and tied one against teams they should have or at least could have beaten. Against the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, though, the Giants showed that they have to be taken seriously – not as a Super Bowl contender, but as a team that has a plausible path to the playoffs and could be a tough opponent for whoever they would meet in the first round.

Let’s take a look at Pro Football Focus grades and advanced stats for the game to see which players helped them get to that point.

PFF grades: Coaching

OK, PFF does not grade NFL coaches, so that title is misleading. Maybe, though, we can get an indirect clue about which teams are well-coached and which aren’t by looking at the overall PFF team grades:

At the top of the PFF overall rankings we see many of the teams that most people would consider the cream of the crop in the NFL this year, most of them with records that support that ranking, e.g., CIN, DET, SF, LAR, JAX, KC. At the bottom we see most of the teams we’d consider the NFL’s worst: MIA, LAC, TEN, IND, ARI. In other words, good/bad players generally make for good/bad teams.

There are outliers, though, and there can be a couple of reasons for that (in my mind):

  • Teams with a few transcendent players and otherwise mediocre talent. The quintessential example is Buffalo, 9-1 but only 11th in overall PFF grade. My interpretation: Josh Allen hides an otherwise middling group with his great play.
  • Teams with considerable talent but poor coaching or game management: I might put the Jets (No. 12 but only 3-8) in that category.
  • On the flip side, teams that aren’t that talented overall but are very well coached: Here we have the Vikings, 19th in overall player grades but 7-3. Last night’s loss to SF notwithstanding, most people acknowledge that the Vikings are where they are mostly due to the tremendous defensive scheme that Brian Flores has created.

Then we have the Giants. They’re even lower than Minnesota in overall player grade (21st in the NFL), yet they sit today at 6-3-1. The conventional wisdom is that the mismatch is explained by their easy schedule to date. Undoubtedly there is some truth in that. However after their victory Sunday, the Giants have now beaten PFF’s No. 5 (HOU), No. 6 (JAX), and No. 8 (DAL) teams as far as individual player performance is concerned. That has to say something about John Harbaugh and the rest of the Giants’ coaching staff.

PFF grades: Offense

You know it wasn’t a great day for the offense when Chris Manhertz is your highest graded offensive player – by a lot (mainly for his 14-yard pass reception on his only target).

As for the passing, it wasn’t J.J. McCarthy’s greatest day. He couldn’t hit the broad side of the barn on his deep passes (0 for 5 beyond 20 yards):

Most of those incompletions, moreover, were way overthrown, especially a couple to poor Darnell Mooney, who was getting open and had little to show for it. McCarthy’s -16.9% completion percent over expected was…awful. As a Viking, McCarthy’s deep passing wasn’t elite, but it wasn’t this bad either, so let’s just call it a bad day at the office. Take away the deep passes and he was at least above 50%. He had one “big-time throw” (BTT) and no turnover-worthy plays (TWP), and in fact he has 11 BTTs and only four TWPs as a Giant. That’s a great ratio. PFF’s leading passer, Joe Burrow (and who would argue this season?), has 21 BTTs and seven TWPs, a pretty similar ratio, in more than twice as many dropbacks as J.J. has. Anyway, how can we criticize McCarthy after he ran down – and successfully tackled – safety Antonio Johnson after Johnson had scooped up Cam Skattebo’s fumble and looked like he was taking it to the house?

With one exception, the pass protection was pretty good Sunday – McCarthy was not sacked at all. Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan Jr., and Sisi Mauigoa had clean stat sheets, while Jermaine Eluemunor gave up only a hit and a hurry. Bryan Hudson, however, had by far his worst game as a Giant, surrendering a QB hit and five hurries.

That said, Hudson graded well in run blocking, while Runyan and Thomas were near-average and Eluemunor and Mauigoa were below-average. Among players who carried the ball, the only notable number is Skattebo’s poor rushing grade, mostly due to his fumble that could have cost the Giants the game.

Malik Nabers was McCarthy’s primary receiving target Sunday, with 7 receptions in 10 targets for 55 yards and a TD and an above-average grade. Isaiah Likely had his quietest game of season with only one catch in 3 targets, but it was for 35 yards, more than half of them after the catch. Malachi Fields had what looks like a mostly nondescript day stat-wise with only two catches in five targets, but his impact on the game was much bigger:

(1) One of them was the 19-yarder between defenders on an absolutely beautiful throw by McCarthy that kept the ball in the Giants hands late in the fourth quarter:

(2) Another was a beautiful 39-yard pass down the left sideline by McCarthy on which Fields drew pass interference near the goal line, leading to a TD finally on a Jameis Winston keeper a few plays later:

This is why you have to take stats of any kind for what they are – one window on performance but not the only one. Those were two great McCarthy throws and two great Fields plays on them, each of them important to the outcome of the game. PFF and other stats venues try to exclude “garbage-time” stats, and PFF does give credit for a well-thrown pass that is broken up due to pass interference, but I’m not sure anyone adequately quantitatively accounts for well-executed offensive plays that draw penalties and that contribute to sealing a victory late in a game.

PFF grades: Defense

The defense was a different story. There were many Giants players who had great games, which makes sense when you hold one the NFL’s best offenses to 18 points.

Abdul Carter had an absolutely spectacular day. PFF gave him a 91.1 overall grade, mostly due to his disruptive pass rush. PFF credited him with two sacks, three QB hits, and four hurries. Next Gen Stats credited him with 12 pressures, leading the league Sunday, with six of those being quick (under 2.5 s) pressures:

Staying on the defensive line, Kayvon Thibodeaux was credited by PFF with 4 pressures, while D.J. Reader continued his excellent season with 5 pressures, including a sack and a QB hit. C.J. Okoye had a QB hit, and Shelby Harris, though grading low overall because of poor run defense, had a QB hit and hurry. Dawuane Smoot contributed 2 hurries. Bobby Jamison-Travis played more poorly than in his last few outings and did not make the stat sheet at all in his 22 snaps.

The Giants’ secondary had an excellent game overall. At the top of the list was Deonte Banks, who received an outstanding grade for good reason – six tackles and an assist with no missed tackles, and only two receptions in 10 targets for 21 yards with an interception and two pass breakups. Paulson Adebo was almost as good, with only two receptions in eight targets, an interception, and a pass breakup. Adebo and Banks were among the best in the NFL Sunday:

Jevon Holland graded highly as well, with one pass breakup. Dru Phillips graded below average overall, because he surrendered seven receptions in 10 targets, but he also broke up two passes, was generally tight in his coverage, even on the Parker Washington non-TD play, and was sticking with receivers better than we’ve seen in recent games. Ar’Darius Washington graded low because one of his two receptions given up in four targets was a TD.

The linebackers had a mostly quiet game. Arvell Reese graded only average overall, but he did have two QB hits and two hurries, along with five tackles and two assists (but one missed tackle). At the other end of the spectrum, Micah McFadden was the lowest graded defensive player, mostly because he missed six tackles. He also gave up seven completions in eight targets for 70 yards.

Advanced stats

Here’s an indication of how much the Giants’ pass rush bothered Trevor Lawrence, and heroic measures he took to avoid it and keep plays alive Sunday:

Lawrence actually had six plays in which he held the ball for more than 5 seconds, once more than 10 seconds. A less athletic quarterback would have been sacked 10 times or more.

Sticking with the defense, here’s how well Abdul Carter and D.J. Reader have played this season, looking at both pass rush (y-axis) and run defense (x-axis) compared other defensive line players around the league:

Here’s a nice aggregated clip of Carter’s pass rushes Sunday:

And here’s a key to watch for the rest of the season. Dennard Wilson has been blitzing a lot in order to create pressure this season, but you’d really not rather do that if you can get pressure with four. Sunday, he was able to:

File this one under “the defense would like to call another witness, Your Honor”:

I mentioned J.J. McCarthy’s awful CPOE earlier, the worst in the NFL (barely) Sunday. His success rate (progress toward a first down or positive EPA) was bad too, and his NFL passer rating of 69.3 was the lowest in the league. Looking beyond these, though, we see that McCarthy’s QBR was actually the sixth-highest in the league Sunday. According to ESPN’s breakdown of the components of QBR, McCarthy led the NFL Sunday in “clutch-weighted” expected points added through rushing, so even though he overthrew all those deep passes (note the league-leading aDOT in the chart above), he also added significant value with his 33 net rushing yards.

On a different topic, speed is always a good thing in the NFL, and the Giants’ new returner, Xavier Gipson, has it:

Finally, with apologies to Jim Mora, it is indeed time to start talking about the playoffs. Unfortunately the Giants have one of the toughest roads to travel as judged by remaining strength of schedule:

Giants fans probably think more about Dallas than anyone else as a threat to a division title, but Washington (which holds the tiebreaker advantage over the Giants) actually has the easiest remaining schedule.

item.title: Eagles vs. Steelers: 19 winners, 8 losers, 4 IDKs
item.description: Let’s talk about that Eagles win!
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles beat the Pittsburgh Steelers!

What did this win accomplish?

Perhaps not much.

Maybe the Eagles merely managed to ruin their draft position in what’s almost surely a lost season.

But more than one thing can be true.

Eagles fans can simultaneously be bummed about missing out on a higher pick … while also enjoying the feeling of their favorite football team winning a game for the first time since September 20. It’s been a long two months!

Or maybe you’re much more on one of those two sides than the other.

Regardless, it’s time to hand out winners, losers, and I don’t knows from this Week 11 win.

For even more analysis, check out my appearance on the PHLY Eagles postgame show.

WINNERS

VIC FANGIO

The Eagles won this game because their defense played much more like the unit we expected to see this season.

Pittsburgh logged just 3.7 yards per play. For context, the Eagles rank dead last in yards per play in 2026 with 4.3.

The Steelers needed 10 possessions to score just 16 points … and three of those came on a two-yard field goal drive that started at the plus 24-yard line due to Jaydon Blue’s kickoff return fumble.

JEREMIAH TROTTER JR.

Trot Jr. led the Eagles in defensive “stops” (tackles that constitute a failure for the offense) with seven, three more than the next closest player. One of those came on the Steelers’ first drive to force a turnover on downs to set up what became a field goal drive at the plus 40-yard line.

Trot Jr. is a very heady player; he often looks like he knows exactly what the offense is going to do on a given play. The combination of his anticipation and physicality makes him a good defender.

JIHAAD CAMPBELL

Second on the Eagles in “stops” in this game? That was Campbell, who turned in his best performance of the season. Campbell’s had some struggles in coverage this year but he only allowed a 80.6 passer rating when targeted in this win.

Maybe the bye week helped him get healthier (though he did injure his finger during this game). And maybe not splitting snaps with Trot Jr. helped his confidence?

BYRON YOUNG

Jordan Davis who?

I’m really not even trying to be disrespectful to the former Eagles defensive tackle. But it’s impossible to not point out that Davis had 1.5 sacks and two TFLs in nine games this season … and Young had two sacks and two TFLs in just 22 defensive snaps played on Sunday.

I know some Eagles film grinders aren’t very big fans of Young. But this was a pretty nice game for the 26-year-old defensive tackle. I don’t know that he’s a future starter for this team but he could be proving useful as a rotational/situational defender.

NOLAN SMITH

Make that six sacks in Smith’s last eight games played.

It sure helped that the Steelers left him unblocked on a blitz in this game.

Still, the production is good to see.

Dating back to Week 5 of the 2024 season, Smith has produced 19.5 sacks, 21 TFLs, and 35 QB hits in 38 games played.

If you take out his lost 2025 campaign where he was still feeling the effects of the triceps injury he suffered in Super Bowl LIX, he has 16.5 sacks, 19 TFLs, and 23 QB hits in a 25-game stretch dating back to Week 5 of the 2024 season.

I realize that’s a cherry-picked parameter. But the larger point about his production stands. He’s making a case to earn a long-term contract extension.

JONATHAN GREENARD

Greenard’s limited snap count suggests that he’s still not close to 100%.

That said, it’s good to see some signs of life from him as it relates to his outlook moving forward. The veteran edge defender is up to two sacks and two TFLs over his last two games after having zero of each in his first five this season.

I have hope that he’s not cooked and this isn’t a total Bryce Huff situation. On that note, he’s only half a sack shy of Huff’s sack total and one TFL shy of Huff’s TFL total with the Eagles!

MARCUS EPPS

Eppsy kept standing out. He absolutely blew up a screen at one point for a TFL. He’s responded well to being benched earlier this year, earning his job back from Kenny Moore II.

QUINYON MITCHELL

Via Next Gen Stats:

Quinyon Mitchell matched up against DK Metcalf 14 times in Week 11, but Metcalf was targeted just twice, failing to haul in either target. Mitchell was in man coverage on 6 of the 14 matchups. Metcalf’s sole reception for two yards came against Cooper DeJean, whom he matched up against 9 times before being ejected from the game for unsportsmanlike conduct late in the third quarter.

Q locked DK up.

Just a shame that he suffered a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter. There seems to be optimism he might be able to play in Week 12. We’ll see.

JONATHAN JONES

The Eagles turned to Jones after benching Riq Woolen for missing multiple tackles. The veteran corner was ready to play, logging three pass deflections, including one to prevent a touchdown in goal-to-go. Jones allowed just a 66.3 passer rating when targeted.

He did get banged up multiple times in this game, which puts his future availability in question.

GABE HALL

It was cool to see Hall notch his first career sack. The Eagles’ 2024 undrafted rookie free agent signing has had a long road to get to this point. But he finally delivered on some of that promise he’s flashed in offseason practices/preseason games.

DARIUS COOPER

The birthday boy was the Eagles’ leading receiver in this win, catching four of his five targets for 59 yards. One of those grabs helped to convert 3rd-and-13 while another converted 3rd-and-10 … both on scoring drives (two Eagles field goals).

The Eagles have not played much winning football this season. When they have, Cooper has made meaningful contributions.

SAQUON BARKLEY

How refreshing was it to see Barkley break a long touchdown run?! A nice little throwback to 2024. Kudos to the Eagles offensive line for blocking up his 38-yard score nicely and kudos to Barkley for running through the Steelers’ defense to find the end zone.

Barkley got banged up later in the game but he ultimately finished with 17 carries for 75 yards (4.4 average). They don’t win this game without him.

Also, pretty wild that Barkley notched his first-ever four-game stretch of his career with at least one rushing touchdown.

DALLAS GOEDERT

A little weird to see Goedert have a season-low in targets with … one. But he made a nice over-the-shoulder grab for 38 yards to convert a 2nd-and-18 and ultimately set up an Eagles field goal.

MARKEL BELL

Entering this game, it felt like T.J. Watt going up against Markel Bell was a MASSIVE mismatch. Bell didn’t totally shut down Watt … but it’s hardly like he got Winston Justice’d out there. Good to see the rookie right tackle hold his own, relatively speaking.

T.J. PAGANETTI

Somewhat of a tongue-in-cheek inclusion because I don’t know how much he really contributed as a consultant who only re-joined the team last week. But the Eagles’ run game did some good things in the first half! Adding him back to the staff probably didn’t hurt.

JAKE ELLIOTT

Elliott is now 11/12 on field goals and 18/18 on extra points this season. And his sole miss came after he previously made a kick that got wiped out by a Jordan Mailata penalty.

Elliott’s biggest kick of his four made field goals against the Steelers was his 55-yarder to give his team a 10-point lead with 4:19 remaining in the fourth quarter. Credit to him for coming up big in the clutch.

BRITAIN COVEY

Covey averaged 13.8 yards on four punt returns. His contributions helped an offense that largely struggled to move the ball.

BRADEN MANN

MVP.

Mann had a sick 70-yard coffin corner punt to pin the Steelers at their own four-yard line.

Pittsburgh then went three-and-out and punted to allow the Eagles to start a drive at their own 45-yard line … which resulted in a FG make.

The value of flipping the field!

MICHAEL CLAY

If the Eagles looked bad on special teams, we’d be ripping their ST coordinator. So, it only feels right to give Clay some credit after the Eagles looked sharp in this regard.

LOSERS

THE STEELERS IN PHILLY

Even in a season when the Eagles are one of the worst teams in the NFL, the Steelers still can’t win in Philly.

The streak dating back to 1965 stays alive.

DK METCALF

Colossal Loser Energy.

He got absolutely locked up by the Eagles’ secondary, which held him to one reception for two yards on four total targets.

Metcalf’s frustration boiled over into after the whistle shenanigans that eventually got him ejected from the game for poking Cooper DeJean in the eyes. Or at least trying to do so.

And then Metcalf denied it as if we didn’t all see it happen!

Lol.

Total clown behavior.

RIQ WOOLEN

Woolen was benched for 33-year-old Jonathan Jones after missing multiple tackles.

He then re-entered the game and was in position to allow a deep catch on a play where Aaron Rodgers overthrew his downfield target.

With Mitchell and Jones getting banged up in this game, the Eagles might have no choice but to put Woolen back out there. But if those two are healthy, he might not get his job back.

Not a very good development for Woolen as he’s set to hit free agency again after this season.

JAYDON BLUE

The Eagles don’t trust him to play on offense and now they likely won’t trust him to play on special teams after fumbling the ball on his sole kick return.

He’s probably going to get cut … again.

SEAN MANNION

The Eagles looked stylistically different on offense with less under center and more shotgun. Is that a sign of the offensive coordinator adjusting on his own? Or was he forced to change? That much is currently unclear.

What we do know is that the offensive output still stunk.

This was not a turning the corner moment coming out of the bye. There were some positive moments in the first quarter, sure, but this was still one of the very worst offensive games in a winning effort this season:

Those six points in the second half?

Three of them came on a six-play, 20-yard field goal drive.

Another came on a nine-play, 34-yard field goal drive. It was their longest drive after halftime.

In other words, the offense is still very bad.

MAKAI LEMON

Lemon dropped two passes in this game. He’s up to six on the season, which ranks tied for second-most in the NFL.

The book on Lemon coming into the pros was that he had great hands. Maybe we’ll eventually see these issues go away, especially if he doesn’t have Joe “Mr. Rocket” Milton throwing missiles at him.

In the meantime, this was a disappointing showing. His three targets resulted in just one reception for three yards.

In the Eagles’ three wins this season, Lemon’s eight targets have produced five receptions for 12 yards and zero touchdowns.

His three most productive games in terms of receiving yards came when the Eagles lost by eight points or more.

The Eagles are 0-6 when he’s targeted at least six times and 3-1 when he’s targeted four or fewer.

ELI STOWERS

The Eagles did not trust Stowers to play a single snap on offense in this game. Not encouraging.

KELEE RINGO

Man, it’s just never happening for Ringo as an NFL defender, is it?

He continues to struggle whenever he gets a rare chance to play on defense.

Logging just seven defensive snaps, Ringo allowed a 20-yard reception to give the Steelers their one and only touchdown.

I DON’T KNOWS

NICK SIRIANNI

I find some of the discourse about Sirianni coming out of this game perplexing.

He saved his job with this win … because Fanigo’s defense looked really good and carried an awful offense?

It’s certainly good to see the team didn’t look checked out. That’s important. And I give Sirianni/Mannion a lot of credit for being aggressive by going for the win on the Eagles’ final drive as opposed to trying to run the ball on third down (instead of passing) and punt it back to the Steelers. That was great to see, even if it didn’t work out. Good process!

But we saw some of the same overly conservative nonsense that’s previously plagued the Eagles. I really didn’t like the offense not even trying to move into field goal range late in the second quarter when they had the ball at their own 30-yard line with 0:54 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. Even if you don’t get into field goal range, you have one of the strongest-armed quarterbacks in the NFL. You could at least try to get in position for a Hail Mary.

And it’s not just about that sequence. The Eagles had a 3rd-and-10 in the third quarter where none of the receivers even ran beyond the marker. They played to set up a 53-yard field goal, which Elliott made. Congrats. But why is the ambition so limited? It’s not like this lack of trust is exclusive to Milton; the Eagles have handled situations similarly with Jalen Hurts in the past.

Anyway, I just don’t know what I really learned about Sirianni and the Eagles in the bigger picture from this game. They beat a pretty bad team while not looking great themselves. It’s fun to enjoy the win in the scope of having a good Sunday. I struggle to see how there’s greater meaning to take away from this result. That is, unless the Eagles build upon it. If they do, we can have a different conservation. If they don’t, who cares?

JOE MILTON

It’s hard not to grade Milton on a curve given that he’s still relatively new to the team and his support system isn’t ideal.

The box score certainly wasn’t sexy: 11/21, 141 yards (6.7 average), 0 TD, 0 INT, 73.7 passer rating … five carries, seven rushing yards.

Milton did complete a pretty awesome throw to Darius Cooper while on the move to his left to turn 3rd-and-13 into a first down on a field goal drive:

He also had nice touch on his 38-yard completion to Goedert. And he made the game-sealing first down completion to DeVonta Smith on the Eagles’ final drive.

So, here’s to crediting him for his first NFL win while also acknowledging he was a big part of the offense largely looking rough. Too many inaccurate throws and too much mustard on some passes.

DEVONTA SMITH

Smitty made the catch that counted most by grabbing the game-winning first down conversion.

It was a rough day on the whole for him, though. He didn’t look to be 100% upon returning from his hamstring injury and his somewhat limited snap count suggested that was the case.

His 12 targets resulted in just five receptions for 41 yards. He wasn’t officially charted with any drops but he failed to secure some catchable passes.

ZACH ERTZ

I was surprised to see that Ertz played six snaps because I really do not recall him being on the field. I don’t know that he’s even going to get the franchise record for all-time receptions when he’s not even playing much, let alone being targeted.

To a larger point, it’s pretty insane that this team is carrying five tight ends on the roster. There’s just no need for that.
