item.title: Fernando Mendoza shows growth despite Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 loss to Denver Broncos
item.description: Winners and losers from Denver, as the rookie quarterback takes a step in the right direction.
item.content:encoded:
The Las Vegas Raiders are struggling to find wins right now, dropping their seventh game in eight weeks with the Week 11 loss to the Denver Broncos. However, the Raiders showed plenty of fight in Denver, battling back from a 17-0 deficit to tie the game late in the third quarter. Of course, Las Vegas still has plenty of work to do to get over the hump, but that does leave more room for optimism in this week’s winners and losers column.

WINNER: Fernando Mendoza

It certainly wasn’t a perfect outing, as there are undoubtedly a few throws Mendoza will want back. The fourth-down miss to an open Jalen Nailor and the fourth-quarter pick-six to Ja’Quan McMillian to end the Raiders’ comeback hopes were the two biggest. However, the No. 1 pick showed plenty of growth from last week, especially with how he handled pressure.

Mendoza did a better job of navigating the pocket and finding his answers to get out of trouble compared to his first start, and week-to-week growth is all the Raiders can ask for at this stage. Also, tossing three touchdown passes, including a 68-yarder to Ashton Jeanty, against one of the NFL’s best defenses over the past few years should help the rookie build some confidence moving forward.

LOSER: Tre Tucker

Mendoza’s stat line (18/37, 267 yards, three touchdowns, one interception) would have looked better had Tucker not let him down. The first instance came early when the wideout won a deep post route but appeared to slow down as the ball was coming, leading to an incompletion. Then, while they weren’t the easiest catches, Tucker had a pair of drops that were momentum killers for the Raiders’ offense.

He did manage to finish with 50 yards, including a 39-yard grab. However, hauling in just two passes on a team-high 10 targets isn’t nearly good enough from the guy who is supposed to be the team’s top wide receiver, especially with Brock Bowers out. Putting it simply, Vegas needed Tucker to step up, and he failed to rise to the occasion.

WINNER: Ashton Jeanty

Heading into the game, Jeanty hadn’t recorded a run of 10 yards or more since Week 4, and he ripped off a 46-yarder in Denver for his longest rush of the season. On top of that, the 2025 first-round pick won deep on a wheel route to haul in a 68-yard touchdown catch for another explosive play.

That led to him finishing as the team’s leading rusher (11 carries for 79 yards) and receiver (five catches for 90 yards), recording the most yards from scrimmage (169) he’s had this year. This is the type of performance many have been waiting for from Jeanty, and one that hopefully is a sign of what’s to come from the Raiders’ duo of young first-rounders in the backfield.

LOSER: Eric Stokes

Was Stokes Las Vegas’ worst defender on Sunday? No, but he continues to fall short of being the reliable coverage defender the secondary needs him to be.

The veteran corner was targeted three times and allowed three completions for 43 yards, according to Pro Football Focus. That brings him up to 460 yards surrendered for the entire campaign, and he’s yielded a 71.5 completion percentage, 213 yards and two touchdowns in the last four games combined.

At this point, the coaching staff needs to consider benching Stokes and seeing what the young guys (Jermod McCoy, Hezekiah Masses and Darien Porter) can do with more opportunities for the rest of the season. The $30 million corner may have signed a contract extension in the offseason, but he’s hurting the team right now and isn’t living up to his end of the bargain.

WINNER: Jack Bech

Bech was listed as a loser last week but responded to the criticism well, registering a career-high 88 receiving yards and his second career touchdown. He was the reliable target the rookie quarterback needed him to be, catching all eight catchable targets, including coming down with a couple of contested catches. The best came on a third-and-13 over the middle, where Bech registered one of his five first-down grabs. He and Mendoza seemed to be in sync against a tough Broncos secondary.

LOSER: Nakobe Dean

While Dean led the team in tackles (12) and managed to record a sack, the box score is deceptive. Per PFF, he was targeted seven times and gave up five completions for 47 yards and a touchdown.

He had an especially tough time in coverage on Denver’s third possession, taking a bad angle that allowed Evan Ingram to turn the corner and convert on a third-and-nine before biting on a play-action fake and leaving his man wide open in the end zone. On top of that, the linebacker registered a 43.8 PFF run defense grade to turn in arguably his worst performance of the season.

WINNER: Running Game

This was touched on a bit with Jeanty; the Raiders had the most success they’ve had on the ground all year, rushing for a season-high 143 yards. Jeanty averaged 7.2 yards per carry, while Mike Washington Jr. had nine carries for 42 yards (4.7 ypc) and Mendoza logged four rushes for 22 yards (5.5 ypc), for a team average of 6.0 yards per rush.

That’s a testament to the offensive line, as the entire unit posted above-baseline (60.0) PFF run-blocking grades, with Trey Zuhn III leading the way at 70.7 and DJ Glaze rounding it out at 63.4. Spencer Burford, who has faced plenty of criticism this season, had a strong performance with a 64.1 mark in the run game and just one pressure allowed on 46 opportunities in pass protection. Also, Michael Mayer managed to post the Raiders’ best PFF run-blocking grade of the afternoon with a 75.4 mark.

Overall, it was a much smoother operation for the Silver and Black’s offense, especially in the running game.

item.title: 17 Winners and 3 losers from the 49ers’ big win over the Vikings
item.description: There weren’t many things to complain about in the 49ers win over Minnesota
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers offense did to the Minnesota Vikings’ defense what they do to every defense. Facing the best defense in the NFL didn’t stop the Niners from being aggressive, nor did they play with one hand tied behind their back—something Brian Flores has made a habit of this season.

On the flip side, the Niners’ defense survived a slow start before they benefited from Minnesota being one-dimensional. It was a statement game for the 49ers, and based on the crowd, it felt like a home game.

Let’s get into the winners and losers from Sunday night football.

Winners

Brock Purdy

Purdy completed 16 of 18 passes against the Vikings’ blitz for 195 yards and two touchdowns. It was the highest completion percentage recorded against a Brian Flores blitz since Lamar Jackson in Week 1 of 2019.

Purdy did not flinch in the face of the blitz. Instead, he attacked it aggressively. Purdy had nine quick attempts. He completed eight of those throws for 108 yards and one score. Purdy averaged 12.4 yards per attempt on quick passes, which was the highest mark against a Flores defense.

Purdy became the first starting quarterback to post a passer rating above 90 against the Vikings. His 146.0 passer rating made Purdy the first player since 2023 (also Purdy) to throw at least three touchdown passes without an interception and post a 145-or-better passer rating in back-to-back games.

Purdy taking only one sack was the story for the 49ers offense. It kept the offense on schedule, which is one of the biggest challenges against a Flores defense.

He did the Houdini thing, running around, buying time, and finding a receiver downfield. Surprisingly, Purdy had no scramble yards. That’s a sign he processed everything quickly enough that he didn’t need to run.

The 34-yarder to Mike Evans was an elite quarterback play and a microcosm of Purdy in this offense. He saw the blitz, knew exactly where to go, and turned a free rusher into an explosive play.

Red zone offense

The best red zone defense in the NFL was no match for the top red zone offense. The 49ers scored on all four trips to the red area.

On their first trip, the Niners sent five eligibles into a route. That left George Kittle 1-on-1 with a linebacker. Kittle crossed his face, broke a tackle, and scored 17 yards later.

The second trip looked like the first trip. It was another route concept with five eligibles on a route from 12 personnel. This time, it was Kittle on a safety. Purdy threw the ball before Kittle turned his head, but the pass hit him in the facemask, leaving Kittle no choice but to catch it.

On the third trip, Mike Evans was matched up against Harrison Smith. Before Evans caught it, Keenan Allen raised his hands, signaling a touchdown.

The final trip capped off a 98-yard drive. Christian McCaffrey ran for 13 yards and then scored on a 6-yard touchdown run.

With Kittle, Evans, and McCaffrey as red-zone options, a defense has few answers. The condensed splits helped dictate matchups.

Mike Evans

Every time Evans plays, it makes you wonder why the Niners don’t throw him the ball every time. Evans finished with six receptions for 109 yards and a touchdown.

Every catch he had resulted in a first down or a touchdown. Evans’ first reception came on 3rd and 1 for 14 yards. He had a 34-yarder on 2nd and 10. On 2nd and 13, Evans gained 29 yards. Add in 10- and 18-yard receptions on 2nd and 7, and you have a walking first down.

Renardo Green

Green is learning on the fly what it takes to become a complete cornerback in the NFL. The days when you could line up in press-man coverage every snap are long gone. You have to tackle, play off coverage, sit in zone, etc. He led the defense with nine tackles. Green kept everything in front of him in Week 11. He was targeted 7 times and only allowed one first-down reception. In total, Green gave up only 29 yards in coverage.

Fred Warner

Warner was second with eight tackles. He didn’t have any forced fumbles, but Warner had a key tackle for loss early in the game and broke up a pass.

You can’t quantify everything. Kirk Cousins had 38 attempts. Only seven of them were over the middle, and two were completed. That is a Fred Warner stat. He took away the most important part of the field in a game that featured mostly passing.

The offensive line

You can’t help but feel some type of emotion after seeing what happened to Colton McKivitz, who is out for the season. McKivitz only played 26 snaps, but he didn’t allow any pressure, and Sumer Sports had McKivitz down for three impact plays. His replacement, Vederian Lowe, came in cold and also pitched a shutout in pass protection.

If you knew the 49ers would only allow one sack and surrender two pressures against the Vikings, you probably would have predicted a blowout win. That’s what happened. Connor Colby responded well a week after Quinnen Williams bullied him. Against Flores, the center generally has a lot on his plate. Jake Brendel looked comfortable, and the Niners’ centers didn’t botch any plays.

Each starter had at least three impact plays, with Dominick Puni and Trent Williams having four. The offense didn’t run it much, but Christian McCaffrey had a 50% success rate, averaging 1.5 yards before contact, including a 10+ yard gain. Only two of McCaffrey’s 12 rushing attempts were stuffed.

The 49ers offensive line continues to excel.

Losers

The third-down defense

One of the few areas where the Vikings found success was on late downs. Their 50 percent third-down success rate ranked in the 71st percentile. The 49ers only forced one three-and-out.

The how is the biggest concern. Upton Stout got mossed on a 3rd and 14. A coverage bust left TJ Hockenson wide open on 3rd and 3. He gained 16 yards. Aaron Jones picked up 13 yards on 3rd & 10. Tai Felton gained eight yards on 3rd and 9, but the Vikings picked up five yards on 4th and 1.

Those were all in the first half, when the game was still within reach. Cousins was 16th out of 22 quarterbacks with at least 25 dropbacks in average time to throw. He’s one of the hardest quarterbacks in the league to sack. It seemed like there was a disconnect on third downs between the coverage and the call. The secondary was too passive. You have to know your personnel. In this case, the quarterback you’re going against. Cousins only needed to throw in a tight window on 18.4% of his dropbacks.

Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout

Stout has physical limitations that make it difficult for him to flourish in coverage. He allowed all three of his targets to be completed for 50 yards. He only rushed the passer twice and didn’t affect Cousins. He also only had two tackles. The good news is two of Stout’s three targets were tight windows, but that doesn’t matter against a 6’5″, 251-pound tight end.

Variance wasn’t on Stout’s side. He only allowed 1.6 yards per separation, so you’d think he’s a candidate for positive regression. You can’t say the same about Lenoir. The box score isn’t bad. Lenoir gave up three catches on seven targets, breaking up multiple passes. He also had a couple of run stops. The forced fumble bailed Lenoir out from allowing a would-be touchdown.

It’s clear that teams are going to hunt him. He was targeted early and often in this game. Lenoir forced a tight window on only two of his seven targets. Those predictive stats don’t give you much confidence that Lenoir can turn things around.

Winners

CJ West

West played 19 snaps, the fewest of any defensive tackle in Week 11. Despite that, he had the most impact plays with four. West looked like a player who wasn’t battling injury and playing himself into shape. Instead, it looked more like the player we saw as a rookie. West had a tackle for loss and two pressures.

Getting help from the interior hasn’t been easy for the 49ers over the past three games. Hopefully, this is a sign of things to come for West.

Osa Odighizuwa

Nobody is happier when a team is forced to stop running the ball than Odighizuwa. He can pin his ears back and do what he does best: rush the quarterback. Odighizuwa posted a 20% pass-rush win rate and a 25% pressure rate against the Vikings. He also split a sack with DeForest Buckner. Only one defensive tackle generated more pressure than Odighizuwa in Week 11, and only three had higher win rates.

Nick Bosa

Bosa is rounding into form after two months off. Bosa had five pressures and a 26.7% win rate, good for fourth this week among all edge rushers. Anything over 10.5% is above league average, so being in the high 20s shows how dominant Bosa was. Again, these are predictive stats, so they suggest sacks should follow soon.

The pressure and havoc created on Cousins

Romello Height had three pressures. Keion White and Mykel Williams had three. Mykel won cleanly and hit Cousins, forcing an overthrow. On Ji’Ayir Brown’s interception, Buckner pushed the center into Cousins’ lap. Buckner finished with 2 pressures.

As a collective unit, the 49ers forced 10 havoc plays, which is in the 66th percentile. The six quarterback hits were in the 68th percentile. The five runs stuffed were also in the 68th percentile. Ultimately, that pressure is what kept the Vikings off schedule and off the scoreboard.

As frustrating as the defense was on late downs, the Vikings averaged 1.11 points per drive. That’s in the 17th percentile.

The safety play

Kyle Shanahan wasn’t lying about playing the safeties until he finds somebody. Malik Mustapha played 47 snaps. Marques Sigle played 45, while Brown played 41. That’s probably the best way to rotate them.

Brown may have earned himself more playing time with a pick-six. He also had a pressure and broke up a pass. It was a great play by him. He also broke up a pass, as did Sigle. Mustapha allowed two receptions for 22 yards, but I think the fact that the safety group didn’t allow a big play is a big reason why the Vikings struggled.

On the pass breakups, there’s a noticeable difference in aggression between the safety group and the cornerbacks. The trio also missed only one tackle.

George Kittle in the red zone and Keenan Allen on third down

Kittle in the low red zone against a linebacker or a safety is automatic. Allen on third down against the fourth-best coverage player is stealing. The mismatches the 49ers can create make them unfair.

Allen in the Jauan Jennings role is already more productive than Jennings. Allen has been excellent in the run game. He’s even better on third downs, where all of his receptions resulted in first downs.

The veteran pass catchers will make a significant difference for Purdy against playoff-caliber opponents, just as they did on Sunday night.

item.title: Details of Tom Jackson’s sudden death emerge
item.description: Officials in Ohio are looking into Tom Jackson’s sudden passing.
item.content:encoded:
Officials in Ohio are looking into Tom Jackson’s sudden passing.

The ESPN icon’s death was reported to the Hamilton County Coroner’s Office over the weekend and an autopsy was performed on Monday, spokespeople for the department confirmed to the California Post.

They added that Jackson was officially pronounced dead at 4:15 p.m. on Nov. 20 at Christ Hospital in Cincinnati.

Further details regarding the 75-year-old’s passing were not made immediately available, as the Hamilton County Coroner’s Office reps said autopsy results are still pending.

Jackson’s longtime friend and broadcast partner Chris Berman initially announced the heartbreaking news on “Sunday NFL Countdown,” calling the death “unexpected” and “a shock.”

“I saw him just two or three weeks ago,” Berman said.

One of Jackson’s former Broncos teammates, Bob Swenson, said in an interview with the Denver Gazette that he too was “stunned” to learn of Jackson’s passing.

“I talked to him every week, sometimes every day,” Swenson said. “I talked to him and he was going back and forth about getting a back operation and then he said he was going to do it. Then I texted him but I wasn’t getting a response the last couple of days.”

Jackson’s death hit the NFL and college football world hard, with tributes pouring in throughout Sunday following Berman’s announcement.

Lee Corso, Jackson’s former coach at Louisville, called Jackson “the best football player I ever had” in a touching statement.

Broncos head coach Sean Payton, meanwhile, gave a game ball to Jackson’s family after Denver’s 38-24 victory over the Raiders.

Jackson played in the NFL from 1973 to 1986 and went on to work for ESPN for 29 years in retirement.

item.title: Giants-Jaguars: 5 plays that led to the Giants’ victory
item.description: Five situations that led to the Giants’ 23-18 victory
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants pulled off the upset, defeating the talented Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, 23-18. Jacksonville was wildly undisciplined in the game; they committed 13 penalties for 107 yards, while out-gaining the Giants by 116 yards. The Giants, though, found a way to finish the pesky Jaguars, who hung around for far too long in the game.

It was Dennard Wilson’s defense that harassed Trevor Lawrence and dictated to Liam Coen’s high-powered offense. Jacksonville mounted a comeback, with their final two drives totaling 135 of their total 354 yards. Coen, however, opted for a field goal with 3:40 left in the game on a fourth-and-goal at the Giants’ eight-yard line.

The Jaguars were down by eight, and that decision cut the score to five points, but the Giants’ offense — who struggled for much of the game — secured a valuable first down that allowed New York to just run the clock out. It was a 19-yard catch by Malachi Fields that all but secured the win. The Giants defeated a good opponent in this wild game; it’s a signature win that showcases the ceiling of this Giants team. Here are five noteworthy plays, or situations, from the win.

Play(s) 1: FIGURE it out

New York has allowed teams to hang around way too often this season, and they did it – once again – against Jacksonville. New York was up 20-6 at halftime, and they received the opening kickoff. Dominic Zvada, after making two 50+ yard field goals, missed a 32-yarder on the opening drive of the second half and then Cam Skattebo fumbled the football away on the second drive of the half, after a ten-play drive at Jacksonville’s 37-yard line. 

The ball security and inconsistency with Zvada have been abysmal in key spots this season, and the issue has made things much more difficult for the Giants all year.

Play(s) 2: Pick city!

The Giants forced an interception on their second defensive drive, and it was their elite communication on the back end – and the comfort of emerging No. 1 CB Tae Banks – who took advantage of the situation. New York sent five with a Fire-Zone blitz, and Banks passed the original outside receiver to Micah McFadden (41) and then sunk underneath the deep cornerback. The pressure and coverage confused Lawrence, who lobbed a lollipop to the young cornerback. New York would kick a field goal after the interception, which got Zvada back on track – he would go to nail two 50+ yard field goals on the right hash, which is noteworthy.

New York’s offense struggled in the second half of the game, but the defense bailed J.J. McCarthy and the unit out. Paulson Adebo, who was in for an injured Greg Newsome II, intercepted Trevor Lawrence after forcing an INC pass on a deep post to Parker Washington:

Excellent job by Adebo. Still, the Giants’ offense looked inept on the ensuing drive; they took an illegal shift penalty and McCarthy was under duress due to free rushers dialed up by Anthony Campenile. Zvada, at least, made this field goal – a 43-yarder from the left hash. 

Play(s) 3: Abdul Carter a game wrecker

Abdul Carter was a GAME WRECKER against Jacksonville, as he said he would be after receiving criticism on social media for his lack of statistical numbers. He utilized his quickness off the snap to consistently threaten and harass the protection and Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Carter is one of the fastest and explosive rushers in the league, but earning sacks have been his one big issue this season – he changed that in this massive win against Jacksonville. 

Play 4: Touchdown or not a touchdown?

The Giants allowed Jacksonville to remain in the game by missing field goals and turning the football over in the third quarter when they had a 20-6 lead. Trevor Lawrence led a nine-play, 49 yard drive where Parker Washington seemingly came down with this touchdown that would have made the score 20-13 with just over 13  minutes left in the game.

However, the refs – despite everyone in the booth disagreeing – said it was NOT a touchdown, so Jacksonville settled for a Cam Little field goal. I personally felt like Washington maintained enough possession when he hit the ground that it was a touchdown, so I was shocked:

Every fan base probably feels this way, but I don’t remember a call like that going so severely against a Giants’ opponent, especially in such a high-leverage situation. But hey – we’ll take it.

Play(s) 5: Malachi Fields 19-yard gain

The Giants’ offense struggled significantly in the second half. New York was up 20-6, and the slippery momentum was TRYING to be seized by Jacksonville, but Dennard Wilson’s defense hardly capitulated until the final two Jacksonville drives. New York NEEDED a play, and McCarthy put a touch pass over the linebacker to rookie receiver Malachi Fields:

Jacksonville had two minutes left, but two runs by Cam Skattebo netted the first down at the two-minute warning, allowing New York to kneel out the win. The Giants’ offense was unspectacular in the 23-18 win, but J.J. McCarthy did enough in significant situations to escape with an important home victory against a good opponent.

item.title: The Detroit Lions are still no one’s favorites because of September
item.description: Detroit has won six straight behind a resurgent defense and potent offense, yet preconceptions keep them under the radar.
item.content:encoded:
For the Detroit Lions, a six-game winning streak, a high-powered offense, and a defense that’s decidedly turned things around since Week 5 isn’t enough to earn consideration from the media as one of the premier teams in the NFL. Despite being atop the NFC North, the Lions aren’t even the team to beat in their own division.

How the Lions continue to fly under the radar on a national level is, on one hand, expected. They can’t outplay their geography. They don’t play in New York or California or Illinois, states home to the three biggest sports media markets in the country. They’re not “America’s Team” or the up-and-comers they were ahead of the 2023 season. The pillars of their team remain unchanged from the beginning of a run that includes three of four seasons where the Lions have started the season 8-2 or better—something the franchise had never done in the 60 seasons prior. No matter what they accomplish, preconceptions plague this team.

They’re still led by the same Jared Goff everyone decided was the NFL’s Charlie-in-the-Box—the gatekeeper for the Island of Misfit Toys. Remember Charlie from Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer? He lives on the Island of Misfit Toys because he’s named “Charlie” instead of “Jack,” believing his name is “all wrong” and that no child would ever want a second-rate Charlie-in-the-Box.

So sure, Jared looks and acts just as good as the real thing, but his name isn’t Joe or Josh, the names of quarterbacks everyone else fawns over in MVP discussions. The teams of Joe and Josh are being carried by elite quarterback play, and their teams’ mediocre defenses be damned: they’re in firm control of their respective divisions.

As for the Lions defense, that’s what’s going to sink their ship this season, just as it did in 2024 when the team went 15-2 and lost to the Washington Commanders in the Divisional Round. According to the pundits, this defense is still the same turnstile it was during the first month of the season, except now its without two of their top defenders in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson—how could Detroit possibly be considered a top-10 team? In fact, their defensive core will not play a single game together this season, so consider their Super Bowl window shattered.

Mind you, we all live in our own echo chambers, seeds planted on a screen where our algorithms grow around us into any shape we encourage it to take: it’s an environment as real as the world. It becomes the truth, it is the truth. So while we play part in creating these environments, it doesn’t excuse these takes as any less misinformed than they actually are. It’s what makes finding the right coverage for football—or anything, really—all that more difficult. Digital literacy is the single most useful tool in protecting our most important currency in today’s day and age: our attention.

If you’re still paying attention, the Lions defense ranks 12th in EPA/play and eighth in success rate since Week 5 per SumerSports. The run defense ranks first in EPA/rush and third in success rate against the run. Their pass defense has creeped its way toward becoming an above-average unit since the return of Brian Branch in Week 7: 12th in EPA/pass and ninth in success rate against the pass. When you put that unit opposite of an offense that ranks sixth in EPA/play and third in success rate this season—fifth in EPA/play and sixth in success rate since Week 5—you can see why they’ve rattled off six wins in a row.

Yet, somehow, it feels like it could all be for naught if Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears leave Ford Field with a win on Thursday. Dan Campbell will make no excuses for his team if they can’t pull off their third win in the past 11 days, but you can count on the talking heads to deem the Bears as the crown jewel of the NFC North, if not the entire conference. But if the Lions, the current underdogs for this Thanksgiving Day showdown, beat the Bears, rest assured, you can count on some special pleading from those defending Chicago’s honor.

item.content:encoded:
It's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule. The Packers and Rams play Wednesday night, while we have the usual three-game Thanksgiving lineup. We also have the Broncos and Steelers on Black Friday, then the normal Sunday slate and Monday Night Football.

So Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers. We're here to help out, taking you through the NFL injury report with the latest updates and some fantasy analysis for key players.

Quarterback

  • Justin Herbert, LAC (concussion protocol)

  • Drake Maye, NE (leg) — Out at least six weeks

  • Sam Darnold, SEA (quad)

Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively. Herbert turned in his first QB1 finish of the 2026 season with 22.44 fantasy points against the Jets on Sunday. He only had 131 passing yards, two TDs, 32 rushing yards and another score on the ground, so it isn't like "we are so back" or anything. But now Herbert will need to clear concussion protocol in order to play Week 12 against the Patriots, another solid matchup.

With how the QB landscape is right now, if Herbert can clear, he isn't a bad add as a QB2 or streaming option for Week 12. The Chargers have some winnable matchups down the stretch and Herbert will likely need to throw. Maybe Herbert and the Chargers can still salvage something for fantasy.

Darnold: The reigning Super Bowl champ has missed the past two games but has a shot to get back on the field for Week 12 against the 49ers in a big spot. Seattle is coming off its bye and Drew Lock has been the starter. He's been more than serviceable, undefeated in essentially four starts this season. There's not much difference between Darnold and Lock starting for fantasy managers. Whoever starts will be a QB2 this week, and either way, Jaxon Smith-Njigba will get fed.

Johnson has RB1 finishes in three of his past four games.

The Chiefs take on the Bills in a highly anticipated matchup on Thanksgiving night. Walker will have a short week to get ready to return, which isn't ideal. If Walker sits again, Johnson can be fired up as an RB1 in what should be a high-scoring affair. If Walker is able to play, we could see him eased back into action given how well Johnson has fared in his stead. In that scenario, Walker would return to RB1/2 status while Johnson would hold value as a flex play.

Tuten: The Jaguars took a tough loss in Week 11 to the Giants and lost Tuten late in the game with an undisclosed injury. He had been dealing with an ankle issue coming into the contest, so it could have something to do with that. Either way, Tuten has been playing pretty banged up over the last handful of games.

If Tuten ends up missing Week 12, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would likely take over the backfield. He had four carries for 28 yards against New York, and has four rushing TDs on the season. item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
item.description: One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.

Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

Ferguson was on track to return earlier this month before suffering a hamstring injury at practice.

But now his ankle has not responded to treatment the way he or the team anticipated.

“Didn’t necessarily feel great, but he had a really good week of practice but you could still see he was kind of getting comfortable,” McVay said of the process with Ferguson, via Adam Grosbard of the Southern California News Group. “Took some meds to be able to do that. Gets the hamstring on a Friday, and then, as he's really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it, and it was like something in his deltoid and his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want.

“I don't know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it's just not coming along, and he wouldn't be able to be himself and put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete, some of the change of direction, moving him across the formation.”

Ferguson is now set to remain on injured reserve for the rest of the year.

A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Ferguson was able to appear in just three games this year, catching seven passes for 63 yards with a touchdown. He caught 11 passes for 231 yards with three TDs in 14 games as a rookie last year.

item.title: Terrance Ferguson out for season, needs ankle surgery
item.description: Per Sean McVay, Terrance Ferguson’s ankle is not improving and requires surgery
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams have suffered another frustrating injury setback, as tight end Terrance Ferguson’s availability for the remainder of the 2026 season is in serious question. What initially appeared to be a routine recovery from an ankle injury has turned into a lengthy absence, with a hamstring injury creating another obstacle just as Ferguson appeared ready to return.

Ferguson originally landed on Injured Reserve after suffering an ankle injury against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. The rookie tight end missed several weeks but appeared to be making progress toward a return in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders.

Unfortunately, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury during Friday’s practice before the Washington Commanders game, just days before he was expected to make his return. Head coach Sean McVay revealed that Ferguson would likely miss another couple of weeks, creating another frustrating setback for the young tight end.

Now, the latest reports indicate Ferguson is still not ready to return, with both his ankle and hamstring continuing to complicate his recovery. McVay acknowledged that Ferguson was not ready to play against Green Bay, although the Rams planned to activate him from Injured Reserve before his 21-day practice window expired.

The situation is particularly disappointing for a Rams offense that desperately needs healthy pass-catching options. With Puka Nacua also facing an extended absence following knee surgery, Ferguson’s potential return could have provided Matthew Stafford with another weapon in the passing game.

For now, Ferguson’s recovery remains a significant concern. After multiple setbacks, the Rams could be forced to finish the season without one of their promising young tight ends.

item.title: Now Terrance Ferguson is done for the year?
item.description: Rams get dealt another blow with Ferguson ruled out for 2026
item.content:encoded:
Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson needs ankle surgery and will be out for the rest of the 2026 season, according to Sean McVay. L.A.’s second-round pick in 2025 was expected to be a prime breakout candidate this year, but he hasn’t played since Week 3 and will finish the season with just seven catches for 63 yards and one score.

The timing couldn’t be worse, as the Rams just put Puka Nacua on season-ending IR and McVay revealed that the team doesn’t expect Davante Adams back any time soon either.

This is a wildly disappointing end to what was seen as a great breakout opportunity for Ferguson, who had flashes of talent during his rookie season, but hasn’t stayed healthy enough to get his second year off the ground. Ferguson now has just 294 yards in two seasons since L.A. traded down in 2025 in order to acquire a 2026 first-round pick that the team used on Ty Simpson.

Neither player has had much of an impact this season.

Ferguson was expected back from his Week 3 injury earlier this season, but he had a setback during while L.A. was preparing for the Washington Commanders. Even with the setback, the Rams had been holding out hope that Ferguson could return sometime this year, which may have been part of the reason they didn’t force a trade at the deadline, choosing instead to go with who they had.

Instead, who the Rams planned on having is no long who they have. With Nacua and Ferguson out, it’s hard to see L.A.‘s passing attacking keeping up with the San Francisco 49ers and other top offenses around the league. The Rams will maybe look at rookie right end Max Klare to fill the void.

Unfortunately, Klare has only played 30 snaps and doesn’t have a target.

What is more likely is that the Rams don’t know who can replace Ferguson, and like they have done with all their injuries throughout the season, they’ll have to figure it out. The question of whether L.A. should go sign Brandon Aiyuk took another turn for the maybe.

item.title: 49ers reportedly release veteran WR Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: Aiyuk will become a free agent if he clears waivers.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers are reportedly releasing veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

This ends the months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

Aiyuk is subject to waivers, but if he clears them, he will be a free agent. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that a spot on the Washington Commanders' practice squad is the likeliest next step for the veteran wide receiver.

After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on Nov. 9, at which time the 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption to decide if they wanted to release him, trade him or add him to the 53-man roster. The reinstatement was the first step toward Aiyuk's eventual release.

Aiyuk's breakup with the Niners is no surprise. Leading up to the 2025 season, reports surfaced that guarantees in his contract were voided amid growing frustrations between the organization and the veteran wideout.

Then, in January, 49ers GM John Lynch officially acknowledged the impending divorce between the two sides, stating in his end-of-season news conference, "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers."

Aiyuk is 28 and hasn't played since Week 7 of the 2024 season. Before his injury, he had spent his entire five-year career with the 49ers.

San Francisco drafted him with the 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He had his breakout season in 2022, finishing with 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns. Aiyuk returned in 2023 and improved, finishing with 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

He suffered his injury in 2024 against the Kansas City Chiefs. This kicked off two years of wide receiver injuries for the 49ers.

San Francisco has been playing this season without Aiyuk in consideration for the roster. As such, the Niners have turned to Deebo Samuel, Mike Evans and Keenan Allen in the passing game, with promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling expected to return from injury soon.

If Aiyuk joins Washington, the Commanders will look to get him up to speed as No. 1 wide receiver Terry McLaurin has been ruled out for the season due to a torn ACL. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams have picked up the slack, but Washington could use Aiyuk if he can play close to his pre-injury level.

item.title: 49ers make final decision on Brandon Aiyuk, ending ugly saga with former star
item.description: The Niners ended the saga that is Brandon Aiyuk.
item.content:encoded:
The bitter saga between the San Francisco 49ers and Brandon Aiyuk has finally come to an end.

San Francisco released Aiyuk on Monday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This means Aiyuk is free to resume his NFL career elsewhere.

The 28-year-old wide receiver has spent his entire career with the 49ers’ franchise after being selected in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft. His first two seasons, he was a solid, complementary piece to the Niners offense.

In 2022, he posted his first season surpassing 1,000 yards receiving. Then in 2023, he had his breakout campaign, reeling in 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. The future appeared bright for the enigmatic receiver.

But the following season Aiyuk sustained a brutal knee injury. He has not played in an NFL game since October 2024..

Aiyuk’s relationship with the 49ers began deteriorating in 2025 over disagreements about how his knee rehab was handled.

San Francisco then voided $27 million in Aiyuk’s future guaranteed salary because of alleged contract violations in Nov. 2025 and placed him on their reserve/left squad list a month later.

Aiyuk spent this past summer making strange social media posts putting the 49ers on blast and demanding his release so he could sign elsewhere.

News broke last month that he sought reinstatement from the NFL, and he met with the 49ers on Nov. 6. The NFL granted his reinstatement three days later, and San Francisco has now released him two weeks after that.

It will be interesting to see whether any team signs Aiyuk, or whether this saga with San Francisco soured Aiyuk’s standing with the NFL’s 31 other teams.

item.title: DK Metcalf ‘can’t remember’ Cooper DeJean incident that led to ejection
item.description: Asked if he believed DeJean provoked him before the interaction, Metcalf said, "You gotta ask him."
item.content:encoded:
Steelers’ DK Metcalf said he has no memory of his alleged eye-poking incident with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean that led to his ejection during Sunday’s 19-16 loss to Philadelphia.

“I can’t remember,” Metcalf told reporters on Monday of his interaction with DeJean during the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field.

When asked if he believed DeJean provoked him before the interaction, Metcalf said, “You gotta ask him.”

At one point, Metcalf denied poking DeJean and explained that he was “just telling [DeJean] to stop pushing me.”

It wasn’t their first scuffle of the game that was initiated by Metcalf.

The 28-year-old wideout was flagged for unnecessary roughness in the first half when he held his block of DeJean well after the play finished.

“I just wish I would have been there for my team,” Metcalf said when asked whether he would’ve handled things differently.

He also told reporters that they’d have to ask his opponents why he struggles to keep his cool during games.

Metcalf, who tallied one catch on four targets for two yards before his ejection, did not speak with the media after Pittsburgh’s loss.

The NFL will review the matter to determine whether Metcalf will face discipline. The Steelers move on to host the Broncos on Friday.

DeJean told reporters that Metcalf “just missed” his eye while discussing the incident after the game.

“We were just competing,” DeJean said. “Things like that happen in football. It wasn’t anything crazy. No one was really saying anything, it was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off of me, things like that. Obviously, it carries over to whatever that was when he got thrown out.

“He wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game. Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me.”

Metcalf has struggled with a lack of production after he signed a four-year, $132 million contract extension with the Steelers in March 2025.

In 10 games, he has recorded a career-low in receiving yards with just 434 on 36 catches with two touchdowns and six drops.

item.title: Falcons cut LB Christian Harris, promote S Jammie Robinson to roster
item.description: Atlanta shuffles the roster coming out of the bye.
item.content:encoded:
Quite often, stories in the NFL that seem destined to unfold one way veer off in a very different direction. When Christian Harris was signed this offseason, the athletic but inconsistent linebacker seemed like an obvious favorite to start next to Divine Deablo as a Jeff Ulbrich reclamation project, with the right measurables and experience to put his career back on track after fading into a backup role with the Houston Texans in 2025.

Instead, Harris was surpassed this summer by day three draft pick Kendal Daniels and fell out of the picture at inside linebacker entirely, settling for limited special teams snaps. Even veteran Josh Woods, himself primarily a special teamer, vaulted Harris on the depth chart, leaving Harris with zero defensive snaps through ten weeks. Now, the team has moved on, and Harris will be hoping to land somewhere where he has a clearer path to playing time.

The team announced the move Monday, with safety and special teamer Jammie Robinson taking his roster spot and 2023 Chicago Bears fifth round cornerback Terrell Smith joining the practice squad to take his spot.

This is one of those moves that likely makes sense for both parties. Atlanta has practice squad linebacker Brian Asamoah as a capable special teamer they can call up if needed and should have Deablo, Daniels, Harold Perkins Jr., and Woods all available for Week 12 against the Vikings; Harris was not so good on special teams that he needed to stick around given that. Harris, meanwhile, is still young enough and has enough starting experience that a linebacker-needy team seems likely to give him a long look in the days to come.

Getting Robinson on the roster just made sense, given that the team has (I believe) used up his practice squad call-ups. Robinson has been a core special teamer since last year and has logged heavy snaps there in all four of his games in 2026, including 73% of the special teams snaps in Week 10 against the Chiefs.

Smith, meanwhile, offers solid size at corner and special teams experience to the practice squad. If we see him in 2026, something has gone awry, naturally.

We wish Harris well, and please do give Smith a warm welcome.

item.title: 49ers to waive Brandon Aiyuk, ending lengthy standoff
item.description: The former first-round draft pick hasn't played in the NFL since 2024, and will be searching for a landing spot after his release from the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers are ending the Brandon Aiyuk saga at last.

San Francisco is waiving Aiyuk after seven seasons, according to multiple reports. The wide receiver has not played a snap in the NFL since 2024, during which he missed the final 10 games of the season with a torn ACL.

Aiyuk did not return to practice in 2025. The 49ers voided his guaranteed money for 2026 last November, citing his failure to attend meetings and participate in other team activities. In December of last year, the team placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list.

During the most recent NFL offseason, Aiyuk publicly advocated multiple times for the 49ers to release him. The wideout posted pictures and videos to social media while wearing Washington Commanders merchandise, called out Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and slammed the 49ers' organization and head coach Kyle Shanahan.

BRANDON AIYUK: WR's Instagram timeline, from 49ers rants to Jayden Daniels jabs

On Nov. 2, 2026, Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus to be his new agent. One week later, he was reinstated to the 49ers. The team received a two-week roster exemption after Aiyuk's reinstatement, which expired on Nov. 23, correlating with his release.

Should Aiyuk clear waivers, he will be a free agent.

Brandon Aiyuk landing spots

Aiyuk, who signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers in 2024, is expected to clear waivers unclaimed. Here are three possible landing spots for the 28-year-old receiver:

Washington Commanders

The Commanders are the clear favorite to land Aiyuk following his release. The wide receiver expressed his desire to join the Commanders throughout the summer, even while he was still technically a member of the 49ers.

ESPN and NFL Media insider Ian Rapoport reported on Monday, Nov. 23 that Aiyuk is expected to land with the Commanders' practice squad after he clears waivers.

Washington is in need of additional depth at receiver after losing veteran Terry McLaurin for the season with a torn patellar tendon. Veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams lead the Commanders' current receiving corps through their first nine games.

Going into their "Monday Night Football" game in Week 11, Diggs and Williams have combined for 64 receptions, 712 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. No other active receiver has more than 14 receptions.

Los Angeles Rams

The Rams' receiving room has been facing significant stress tests to its depth thanks to injuries. Veteran star Davante Adams is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and has been out since mid-October. Star Puka Nacua is out for the season after needing to undergo a procedure to repair his MCL.

Shortly after news of the 49ers' planned release of Aiyuk, the Rams also announced that tight end Terrance Ferguson will be out for the rest of the season. The second-year pass-catcher had been out since late September with an ankle injury that ultimately required surgery.

Los Angeles' top healthy receivers going into their "Thanksgiving Eve" game on Wednesday, Nov. 25 are Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels and Tutu Atwell. While the Rams still have tight ends Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson, none of their active wideouts have more receptions this year than Mumpfield's 14.

Houston Texans

Houston is 4-2 after its 0-4 start to the season, which means the Texans are still alive in the AFC playoff picture.

The Texans, like the Commanders and Rams, have had their wide receiver depth tested in the first half of the season. Second-year Jayden Higgins is out for the season after sustaining a torn ACL in training camp. Fellow second-year Jaylin Noel is also out for the season with a turf toe injury he suffered at the end of October. Midseason acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. has missed two straight games with a hamstring injury, and Kayshon Boutte missed time in Week 11 with a hip injury.

The AFC South contenders did just get Tank Dell back after he missed the entirety of the 2025 season, which helps. Houston could still use more help, especially if it hopes to make a playoff push after a brutal start to this year.

What happened to Brandon Aiyuk?

Aiyuk sustained a torn ACL and MCL in Week 7 of the 2024 season. He missed the remainder of that year as a result but was expected to return to action in 2025.

San Francisco tight end George Kittle told Barstool Sports podcast "Pardon My Take" in June that he saw Aiyuk on the field and running some time between Weeks 6-8 during the 2025 season.

"I watched him run over 22 miles an hour and stop on a dime," Kittle said. "So he's still got it."

However, communication between the 49ers and the former first-round pick broke down at some point during the season, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan. The receiver "stopped answering anyone's phone calls, including the head coach's," reported Matt Barrows of The Athletic in January.

"That's something I'd never seen in 22 years of coaching," Shanahan said, per Barrows.

The 49ers voided Aiyuk's guaranteed money for 2026 last November, then placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December. The Athletic reported at the time that Aiyuk had "failed to attend meetings and declined to participate in other team activities."

General manager John Lynch told reporters in January, "I think it's safe to say [Aiyuk]'s played his last snap with the 49ers."

The wideout spent much of the offseason publicly requesting his release from the 49ers so he could sign with another team, specifically the Commanders.

Ultimately, his release did not come until after he hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to represent him earlier this month. The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9, and they waived him two weeks later, on Nov. 23.

Brandon Aiyuk injury

In Week 7 of the 2024 season, Aiyuk tore his ACL and MCL during a game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Aiyuk missed the remainder of the season while recovering from the injury.

Brandon Aiyuk has been ruled out vs. the Chiefs after suffering an apparent knee injury. https://t.co/pWa5Lujy69

— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 20, 2024

According to Kittle, Aiyuk was healthy enough to "run over 22 miles an hour and stop on a dime" by the midway point of the 2025 season. Aiyuk's absence for the entirety of the 2025 season, according to Shanahan and Lynch, was more a result of his refusal to show up for meetings and team activities.

The receiver is expected to be fully healthy, now that he is two years removed from his knee injury. The main concerns for a team looking to sign Aiyuk will come down to his conditioning and readiness to join another NFL roster. After a full year spent away from football, those are not given quantities.

This story will be updated.

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s ‘most likely destination’ is the obvious landing spot after the 49ers release him
item.description: Brandon Aiyuk’s days with the 49ers are officially over
item.content:encoded:
The day we knew was coming is finally here. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the San Francisco 49ers will release Brandon Aiyuk on Monday. After the Niners were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk, the move will likely post on Monday’s transaction wire. That will allow Aiyuk to sign wherever he wants. He has not played in the NFL since October 2024.

Ian Rapoport hinted that the Washington Commanders will be Aiyuk’s next destination. Aiyuk and his former college teammate, Jayden Daniels, reportedly patched things up after Aiyuk’s comments this summer.

Washington, 3-5-1, might be the only team that wants to deal with Aiyuk’s antics. He’ll need to prove he’s even 80% of what he was two years ago. It’s been a long, long time since Aiyuk has played football. So it’s not surprising that interest might be limited when it comes to where Aiyuk could land.

Aiyuk is subject to waivers. Schefter said Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said, “We are looking forward to finding his next team.”

If you’re Robert Saleh and the Titans, wouldn’t you help your rookie quarterback? The same is true for Arizona, which has a head coach who was on the 49ers’ offensive staff when Aiyuk was on the roster.

We’ll keep an eye on where Aiyuk lands, whether he makes a roster, and if he steps foot on a field this season.

item.title: Ja’Quan McMillian is the best ballhawking cornerback in Denver since Aqib Talib
item.description: The Denver Broncos have to find a way to extend the best ballhawking cornerback in the orange and blue since Aqib Talib.
item.content:encoded:
There should be no debate who the best ballhawking cornerback is on the Denver Broncos. Pat Surtain II is the best cornerback in the NFL. Riley Moss is the best number two cornerback in the NFL. That doesn’t change the fact that Ja’Quan McMillian is the best ballhawk in the NFL.

This is the closest recreation of the ‘No Fly Zone’ we’ve seen since that group was winning Super Bowl 50. I don’t see how Denver let’s McMillian walk in March either. They have to find a way to keep this group together.

Saw this comment somewhere on the site:

Since 2023, no player has done all of the following except for McMillian:

10+ sacks

20+ TFLs

30+ passes defended

That is an insane stat line for a slot corner. But the ballhawk mentality goes well beyond just racking up stats. It’s how and when he is making his biggest plays.

McMillian makes the clutch game-changing play at a freakishly high rate and a big reason why the Broncos are known as the most clutch team in NFL history over the last two years. I went back through our X feed for the video of his biggest plays and found time and again those game altering moments where the Broncos’ were on the verge of letting a game slip away and McMillian stepped in to steal all of the momentum back for Denver to preserve or take the lead.

If the Broncos’ front office needs any help deciding if McMillian is worth what he’s asking, they need only look at all of the games they would have lost without a big play he made at the most critical moments:

item.title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Saints
item.description: A win is a win, but it’s even better when almost everyone comes out healthy. Here are @Bryan Orenchuk’s 3 reasons why the Bears came away with the W.
item.content:encoded:
Another somewhat sloppy win, but a win nonetheless.

While it seemed the Chicago Bears missed ample opportunities to score more points against the New Orleans Saints, the most important thing is that Chicago came away with a W and remained healthy in the process.

That said, let’s get to my top 3 reasons Chicago won.

Considering the Chicago Bears are on the verge of a certain level of success the franchise hasn’t experienced in decades thanks to Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, I am going to leave them out of this piece from now on – as it is a given that both were instrumental to Chicago’s success. Go ahead and throw in All-World DT Jeffery Simmons into that category too as he continues to dominate and play at a Defensive MVP level.

So who or what contributed to the win outside of those three? Glad you asked.

1. Defensive Line

One cannot discuss the Chicago Bears defensive line without mentioning the elite level of play by Jeffery Simmons. But what doesn’t get discussed enough is just how much better his supporting cast is playing since Simmons became a Bear. Grady Jarrett finally resembles the player Ryan Poles traded for and should have been awarded a half sack when he and Simmons converged on a retreating Tyler Shough. His activity has been noticeable and continues to create pressure against both the run and pass.

Meanwhile, Montez Sweat is once again looking like the player Chicago acquired when he first arrived from Washington and has had his best three games of the season, matching his sack totals and surpassing his tackle totals from the first five games of the season. Sweat’s sack that resulted in a safety was without Jeffery Simmons on the field too, but it isn’t just sacks and tackles that Sweat is bringing – he made multiple plays on Sunday with his awareness and pursuit/contain that led to big plays of others on the defense. Then we have Austin Booker, who flat-out looks like a legit starting-caliber defensive end on all three downs. Forcing pressure on passing plays and blowing up run plays all across the line of scrimmage to constantly hustling all over the field and getting his hands on the football or recovering loose balls. If these three players can continue to thrive while Shemar Turner and Dayo Odeyingbo return to full health, Chicago’s DL may actually be a strength of this team.

2. Rookies

Bears first-round pick Dillon Thieneman continues to show why he was drafted so high. His pursuit in run support and in the passing game after the catch has been special. And his awareness to fall off his receiver and snag the errant throw by Tyler Shough was a savvy play, especially for a first year player. But it was also the play of rookies Sam Roush and especially Zavion Thomas that caught my eye against New Orleans. Roush had his most complete game as a pro as he continues to see extra playing time filling in for injured veteran Cole Kmet. His blocking continues to improve and he hauled in his only target for 19 yards on a heady scramble drill catch by Caleb Williams. If Roush can continue to improve – especially as a blocker – Chicago’s offense should get back on track sooner or later.

Now if Zavion Thomas continues to ascend like he showed on Sunday, the Bears offense can reach a whole new level! Thomas was Chicago’s most explosive and effective weapon against the Saints and he continues to return kicks. As this young man’s confidence continues to rise, expect some game-changing plays to come from him. And considering the remainder of Chicago’s schedule, those will likely be pretty clutch plays as well. Have to shout out Jordan van den Berg as well, who appeared to put his best tape out there in limited (10 snaps) action.

3. Reserve DBs

Both Clark Phillips III and Cam Lewis continue to make the most of their opportunities in the starting lineup and both made huge plays for the Bears on Sunday against New Orleans. The 24-year-old Phillips might be the savviest acquisition of the year for Poles as Chicago navigates the undependable Kyler Gordon and the need for a versatile slot corner. Phillips had 4 tackles, a FF, Sack, TFL, and pass defended on Sunday and is bringing a much-needed jolt of energy when he is on the field.

Cam Lewis also continues to impress and was all over the field with 5 solo tackles (7 total), 1 sack, 1 TFL 1 PD and 1 QB hit. While Dennis Allen has found himself in a position to create pressure without bringing any linebackers or defensive backs, it is a huge boost when these smaller and quicker players can time up a pass rush well and get to the QB.

item.title: It’s time to consider Brandon Aiyuk for the Rams
item.description: Aiyuk is now a free agent, after the 49ers released him on Monday
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers released Brandon Aiyuk on Monday, ending their relationship with the receiver once and for all. With the Los Angeles Rams desperately in need of help at the position following serious injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, will Sean McVay consider signing Aiyuk to help the team make a playoff push in the final seven weeks?

The Washington Commanders have long been considered Aiyuk’s preferred destination if he got his release from the 49ers, but there’s no reason to believe the Rams couldn’t convince him with a spot on the 53-man roster if that’s what McVay and Matthew Stafford want the team to do.

Aiyuk last played in the NFL in 2024, when he caught 25 passes for 374 yards in seven games. The previous season, Aiyuk had 1,342 yards for the 49ers. He signed a four-year, $120 million contract after that season, but that’s when things went south for the player and his relationship with the team.

After sitting out 2025, Aiyuk is looking for a second chance in the NFL. He hired agent Drew Rosenhaus recently to help him end his contract with the 49ers, which the team finally gave into on Monday.

It’s improbable that Aiyuk would be able to play in an NFL game this month. He hasn’t even practiced in two years. It may be a stretch to think he could even play this year. However, what if the Rams gave him a month to warm up and then were able to put him into a game as soon as Week 16 against the Seahawks? If L.A. is able to stay in the playoff race until then, Aiyuk may be able to help the Rams when they need it the most.

Aiyuk may also like the opportunity to face the 49ers in the playoffs if L.A. makes it that far. Stafford would surely like options other than Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell at the position, if he can help it.

The Rams are not known to be in line for Aiyuk at this time. But now that he’s a free agent, maybe they should consider it.

Unfortunately, he missed time on Sunday while battling the injuries, leading to just a 43% snap share and 13 touches for 53 scoreless yards in the loss. 

If the Jaguars are serious about contending for a Super Bowl, they need their star runner healthy for the stretch run, which makes you wonder if they will ever give him a week off. This week's matchup with the Titans seems like the perfect opportunity to get Tuten some rest, since Jacksonville is 14.5-point favorites.
